source_arguments.name: RHTower.d4BM_actualFirstStokesHorizontalCurrent_eq_canonical
source_arguments.statement:
theorem d4BM_actualFirstStokesHorizontalCurrent_eq_canonical
    (Z : D4BMExteriorCuspCoordinate)
    (P Q : D4BMEisensteinAbsoluteConvergenceParameter) :
    d4BMActualFirstStokesHorizontalCurrent Z.1 P Q =
      d4BMCanonicalFirstStokesHorizontalCurrent
        (P.s - 1 / 2) (Q.s - 1 / 2) Z.1.x (d4BMExteriorCuspHeight Z)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem d4BM_actualFirstStokesHorizontalCurrent_eq_canonical
    (Z : D4BMExteriorCuspCoordinate)
    (P Q : D4BMEisensteinAbsoluteConvergenceParameter) :
    d4BMActualFirstStokesHorizontalCurrent Z.1 P Q =
      d4BMCanonicalFirstStokesHorizontalCurrent
        (P.s - 1 / 2) (Q.s - 1 / 2) Z.1.x (d4BMExteriorCuspHeight Z)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hP :=
    d4BM_actualCompletedPoincareFullSecondJet_eq_canonicalCuspFullSecondJet Z P
  have hQ :=
    d4BM_actualCompletedPoincareFullSecondJet_eq_canonicalCuspFullSecondJet Z Q
  unfold d4BMActualFirstStokesHorizontalCurrent
    d4BMCanonicalFirstStokesHorizontalCurrent
  simpa [d4BMActualCompletedPoincareFullSecondJet,
    d4BMActualCompletedPoincareFullFirstJet] using
      congrArg₂ (fun a b : D4BMFullSecondJet =>
        2 * a.first.value * b.first.value * a.first.horizonX -
          a.first.value ^ 2 * b.first.horizonX) hP hQ

theorem coefficientPattern_isUnit_actual_of_normalized
    {row ι : Type*} [Fintype row] [DecidableEq row]
    {orders : ι → ℕ}
    (base : row → ℂ) (degree : row → ℕ)
    (jetExponent : row → ((Σ i, Fin (orders i)) →₀ ℕ))
    (normalized actual : row → (Σ i, Fin (orders i)) → ℂ)
    (hactual : ∀ r s, actual r s = (s.2.1.factorial : ℂ) * normalized r s)
    (hnorm : IsUnit (Matrix.of fun r b =>
      base r ^ degree b * (jetExponent b).prod (fun s e => normalized r s ^ e) :
      Matrix row row ℂ)) :
    IsUnit (Matrix.of fun r b =>
      base r ^ degree b * (jetExponent b).prod (fun s e => actual r s ^ e) :
      Matrix row row ℂ)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem coefficientPattern_isUnit_actual_of_normalized
    {row ι : Type*} [Fintype row] [DecidableEq row]
    {orders : ι → ℕ}
    (base : row → ℂ) (degree : row → ℕ)
    (jetExponent : row → ((Σ i, Fin (orders i)) →₀ ℕ))
    (normalized actual : row → (Σ i, Fin (orders i)) → ℂ)
    (hactual : ∀ r s, actual r s = (s.2.1.factorial : ℂ) * normalized r s)
    (hnorm : IsUnit (Matrix.of fun r b =>
      base r ^ degree b * (jetExponent b).prod (fun s e => normalized r s ^ e) :
      Matrix row row ℂ)) :
    IsUnit (Matrix.of fun r b =>
      base r ^ degree b * (jetExponent b).prod (fun s e => actual r s ^ e) :
      Matrix row row ℂ)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  let A : Matrix row row ℂ := Matrix.of fun r b =>
    base r ^ degree b * (jetExponent b).prod (fun s e => normalized r s ^ e)
  let scale : row → ℂ := fun b => jetMonomialFactorialScale (jetExponent b)
  have hscale : ∀ b, scale b ≠ 0 := fun b => jetMonomialFactorialScale_ne_zero _
  have hdiag : IsUnit (Matrix.diagonal scale) := by
    rw [Matrix.isUnit_diagonal, Pi.isUnit_iff]
    intro b
    exact isUnit_iff_ne_zero.mpr (hscale b)
  have hmul : IsUnit (A * Matrix.diagonal scale) := hnorm.mul hdiag
  have heq : A * Matrix.diagonal scale = Matrix.of fun r b =>
      base r ^ degree b * (jetExponent b).prod (fun s e => actual r s ^ e) := by
    ext r b
    rw [Matrix.mul_diagonal]
    change (base r ^ degree b *
      (jetExponent b).prod (fun s e => normalized r s ^ e)) * scale b =
        base r ^ degree b *
          (jetExponent b).prod (fun s e => actual r s ^ e)
    rw [jetMonomial_actual_eq_factorialScale_mul_normalized
      (jetExponent b) (normalized r) (actual r) (hactual r)]
    simp only [scale]
    ring
  rw [heq] at hmul
  exact hmul

# Actual Weil pole entry barrier: two failed propagation tests

**Status: exploratory numerical evidence, not a mathematical or Lean proof.** No numerical result from this folder is used in Lean. RH and the actual pole-energy sign remain open.

## Mathematical question

The direct target is nonnegativity of the actual even Weil pole energy `Y(a)`. Together with the actual odd signs, this closes the existing pole-positivity → integrated prime-error bound → resolvent → RH chain.

Inside a late prime-power gap, write `v=Y'`, `F=Y''>0` and consider

`B=Y-v²/(2F)`.

A proof of `B≥0` would imply `Y≥0`, and `B=Y` at an interior minimum. Between entries, differentiation gives `B'=v²F'/(2F²)`. At the entry `a=log(n)/2`, the exact corpus atom laws give continuous value and one-sided curvature, and a velocity jump `v_after=v_before-J`, with

`J=4Lambda(n)(1+1/sqrt(n))²`.

Thus

`Delta B=J(2v_before-J)/(2F)`.

Two proposed direct proofs were tested:

1. Every actual entry preserves or increases `B`.
2. If some entries decrease `B`, all their decreases can be paid by the initial barrier and continuous growth, without needing positive jump contributions.

Both mechanisms fail in the evaluated actual source. Positivity of `B` itself is a separate unresolved claim.

/-!
# Polynomial moments of literal coprime deletion polygons

For actual moduli `P=p+1` and `Q=q+1`, join the successive prefix endpoints
`(n mod P,n mod Q)` by straight segments. Their velocities are exactly the existing
Euler-deletion coefficients, and one common period is a closed polygon.

CRT factors every polynomial segment density into two explicit one-coordinate phase sums.
All coefficient-degree-at-most-three polynomial one-forms have zero circulation. The
higher moment `integral x*y^3 dx` is exactly `P*(P-1)*Q*(Q-1)*(Q-2)/120` for coprime
`P,Q`. In particular the literal moduli-2-and-3 path gives the closed value `1/10`.

This is a finite unweighted arithmetic statement. It supplies no assertion about a weighted
infinite product, no vanishing at a zeta zero, and no RH implication. Polynomial-moment
and path-signature methods have published ancestry; no global novelty claim is made here.
-/

open scoped BigOperators
namespace RHTower.DeletionJointPolygon
noncomputable section

/-- Velocity of the literal modulus `p+1` deletion path. -/
def velocity (p n : ℕ) : ℝ := blockDeletionCoefficient (p+1) (n+1)

/-- Straight interpolation of the exact residue-valued prefix. -/
def position (p n : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ := (n % (p+1) : ℕ) + t * velocity p n

/-- Polynomial one-form integrated along one full common period. -/
def circulation (p q a b : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ t in (0:ℝ)..1, ∑ n ∈ Finset.range ((p+1)*(q+1)),
    position p n t ^ a * position q n t ^ b * velocity p n

/-- Position moments across one coordinate's phases. -/
def phaseMoment (p k : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∑ j ∈ Finset.range p, ((j:ℝ)+t)^k) + ((p:ℝ)*(1-t))^k

/-- Velocity-weighted position moments across one coordinate's phases. -/
def velocityMoment (p k : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∑ j ∈ Finset.range p, ((j:ℝ)+t)^k) - (p:ℝ)*((p:ℝ)*(1-t))^k

theorem velocity_of_lt {p n : ℕ} (hn : n < p) : velocity p n = 1 := by
  have hd : ¬ p+1 ∣ n+1 := Nat.not_dvd_of_pos_of_lt (Nat.succ_pos n)
    (Nat.succ_lt_succ hn)
  simp [velocity, blockDeletionCoefficient, hd]

theorem velocity_last (p : ℕ) : velocity p p = -(p:ℝ) := by
  simp [velocity, blockDeletionCoefficient]

theorem position_of_lt {p n : ℕ} (hn : n < p) (t : ℝ) :
    position p n t = (n:ℝ)+t := by
  simp [position, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (Nat.lt_succ_of_lt hn), velocity_of_lt hn]

theorem position_last (p : ℕ) (t : ℝ) : position p p t = (p:ℝ)*(1-t) := by
  simp only [position, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (Nat.lt_succ_self p), velocity_last]
  ring

theorem velocity_periodic (p : ℕ) : Function.Periodic (velocity p) (p+1) := by
  intro n
  exact congrArg (fun z : ℤ => (z:ℝ))
    (DeletionCoprimeWords.shifted_deletion_periodic (p+1) n)

theorem position_periodic (p : ℕ) (t : ℝ) :
    Function.Periodic (fun n => position p n t) (p+1) := by
  intro n
  simp only [position, Nat.add_mod_right, velocity_periodic p n]

theorem sum_position_pow (p k : ℕ) (t : ℝ) :
    (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (p+1), position p n t ^ k) = phaseMoment p k t := by
  rw [Finset.sum_range_succ, position_last]
  unfold phaseMoment
  congr 1
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun n hn => by rw [position_of_lt (Finset.mem_range.mp hn)])

theorem sum_position_pow_velocity (p k : ℕ) (t : ℝ) :
    (∑ n ∈ Finset.range (p+1), position p n t ^ k * velocity p n) =
      velocityMoment p k t := by
  rw [Finset.sum_range_succ, position_last, velocity_last]
  unfold velocityMoment
  have hs : (∑ n ∈ Finset.range p, position p n t ^ k * velocity p n) =
      ∑ n ∈ Finset.range p, ((n:ℝ)+t)^k := by
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro n hn
    rw [position_of_lt (Finset.mem_range.mp hn), velocity_of_lt (Finset.mem_range.mp hn), mul_one]
  rw [hs]
  ring

/-- The starting coordinate is the actual sum of previous deletion jumps. -/
theorem position_zero_eq_prefix (p n : ℕ) :
    position p n 0 = (deletionCoeffPartialSum (p+1) n : ℝ) := by
  simp only [position, zero_mul, add_zero, deletionCoeffPartialSum_eq_mod, Int.cast_natCast]

/-- Consecutive straight segments meet at their endpoints. -/
theorem segment_endpoint (p n : ℕ) : position p n 1 = position p (n+1) 0 := by
  have h : deletionCoeffPartialSum (p+1) n + blockDeletionCoefficient (p+1) (n+1) =
      deletionCoeffPartialSum (p+1) (n+1) := by
    exact (Finset.sum_range_succ _ _).symm
  rw [deletionCoeffPartialSum_eq_mod, deletionCoeffPartialSum_eq_mod] at h
  have hr := congrArg (fun z : ℤ => (z:ℝ)) h
  simpa only [position, velocity, one_mul, zero_mul, add_zero, Int.cast_add, Int.cast_natCast] using hr

/-- A common period returns both literal coordinates to the origin. -/
theorem common_period_closed (p q : ℕ) :
    position p ((p+1)*(q+1)) 0 = 0 ∧ position q ((p+1)*(q+1)) 0 = 0 := by
  simp [position]

/-- CRT factors the actual segment integrand; no averaging approximation is used. -/

/-!
# Ordered monoid and group homomorphisms

This file defines morphisms between (additive) ordered monoids.

## Types of morphisms

* `OrderAddMonoidHom`: Ordered additive monoid homomorphisms.
* `OrderMonoidHom`: Ordered monoid homomorphisms.
* `OrderAddMonoidIso`: Ordered additive monoid isomorphisms.
* `OrderMonoidIso`: Ordered monoid isomorphisms.

## Notation

* `→+o`: Bundled ordered additive monoid homs. Also use for additive group homs.
* `→*o`: Bundled ordered monoid homs. Also use for group homs.
* `≃+o`: Bundled ordered additive monoid isos. Also use for additive group isos.
* `≃*o`: Bundled ordered monoid isos. Also use for group isos.

## Implementation notes

There's a coercion from bundled homs to fun, and the canonical notation is to use the bundled hom as
a function via this coercion.

There is no `OrderGroupHom` -- the idea is that `OrderMonoidHom` is used.
The constructor for `OrderMonoidHom` needs a proof of `map_one` as well as `map_mul`; a separate
constructor `OrderMonoidHom.mk'` will construct ordered group homs (i.e. ordered monoid homs
between ordered groups) given only a proof that multiplication is preserved,

Implicit `{}` brackets are often used instead of type class `[]` brackets. This is done when the
instances can be inferred because they are implicit arguments to the type `OrderMonoidHom`. When
they can be inferred from the type it is faster to use this method than to use type class inference.

### Removed typeclasses

This file used to define typeclasses for order-preserving (additive) monoid homomorphisms:
`OrderAddMonoidHomClass`, `OrderMonoidHomClass`, and `OrderMonoidWithZeroHomClass`.

In https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/10544 we migrated from these typeclasses
to assumptions like `[FunLike F M N] [MonoidHomClass F M N] [OrderHomClass F M N]`,
making some definitions and lemmas irrelevant.

## Tags

ordered monoid, ordered group
-/

When possible, instead of parametrizing results over `(f : α →+o β)`,
you should parametrize over
`(F : Type*) [FunLike F M N] [MonoidHomClass F M N] [OrderHomClass F M N] (f : F)`. -/
structure OrderAddMonoidHom (α β : Type*) [Preorder α] [Preorder β] [AddZeroClass α]

Product : ℚ := 2/3

/-- **The raw double large sieve is inapplicable here**, and the deficit it must overcome is `N^{1/3}`
— which is precisely what Bombieri–Iwaniec's spacing analysis supplies. -/
theorem raw_double_sieve_inapplicable :
    0 < sieveEfficiencyProduct ∧ bilinearTrivial < doubleSieveOutput ∧ pointsPerBox < 0 :=
  ⟨sieve_inefficient, doubleSieve_worse_than_trivial, subdivision_degenerates⟩


/-!
### Recalibration: progress measured from the raw sieve

On the normalised sum of Theorem 82 (exponents in `L = N^{1/3}`):

    raw double large sieve   :  L²          (Theorem 87)
    trivial bound            :  L¹
    Bourgain's record        :  L^{13/14}   (since `L^{3/2}·L^{13/14} = L^{17/7} = N^{17/21}`)
    Lindelöf                 :  L^{o(1)}

Measured from the **trivial** bound the record has covered `1 − 13/14 = 1/14 ≈ 7 %` of the way to
Lindelöf.  Measured from the **raw sieve** — the actual starting point of the Bombieri–Iwaniec method,
before any spacing analysis — it has covered

    (2 − 13/14) / 2  =  (15/14)/2  =  **15/28 ≈ 53.6 %** .

The discrepancy is exactly the factor `L` by which the raw sieve is worse than trivial: the spacing
analysis first has to climb back to the trivial bound, and only then begins to save.
-/

/-- Normalised-sum exponent (in `L`) of the raw double large sieve. -/
def normRawSieve : ℚ := 2

/-- Normalised-sum exponent of the trivial bound. -/
def normTrivial : ℚ := 1

/-- Normalised-sum exponent of Bourgain's record. -/
def normBourgain : ℚ := 13/14

/-- Normalised-sum exponent of the Lindelöf hypothesis. -/
def normLindelof : ℚ := 0

/-- **Bourgain's record restores to `N^{17/21}`.** -/
@[simp] theorem normBourgain_restores : (3/2 : ℚ) + normBourgain = 17/7 := by
  unfold normBourgain; norm_num

/-- Progress measured from the trivial bound. -/
def progressFromTrivial : ℚ := (normTrivial - normBourgain) / (normTrivial - normLindelof)

@[simp] theorem progressFromTrivial_eq : progressFromTrivial = 1/14 := by
  unfold progressFromTrivial normTrivial normBourgain normLindelof; norm_num

/-- Progress measured from the raw sieve. -/
def progressFromRawSieve : ℚ := (normRawSieve - normBourgain) / (normRawSieve - normLindelof)

@[simp] theorem progressFromRawSieve_eq : progressFromRawSieve = 15/28 := by
  unfold progressFromRawSieve normRawSieve normBourgain normLindelof; norm_num

/-- **From the raw sieve, more than half the required saving has been achieved.** -/
theorem majority_achieved_from_raw : 1/2 < progressFromRawSieve := by
  rw [progressFromRawSieve_eq]; norm_num

/-- **And the two measures differ by the factor `L` separating the raw sieve from trivial.** -/
theorem baselines_differ : progressFromTrivial < progressFromRawSieve := by
  rw [progressFromTrivial_eq, progressFromRawSieve_eq]; norm_num

/-- The remaining saving, from the record to Lindelöf. -/
@[simp] theorem remaining_saving : normBourgain - normLindelof = 13/14 := by
  unfold normBourgain normLindelof; norm_num

For a four-dimensional topological AdS black hole with modular hyperbolic horizon, the quadratic
Einstein--Klein--Gordon stress tensor multiplies horizon Eisenstein modes.  Its angular spectral

regularized triple product.

For `E(z, 1/2 + u)`, the full-level formula of Zagier and Michel--Venkatesh is, up to the stated
normalization,

```text
integral^reg E(u1) E(u2) E(u3)
  = product_{epsilon2,epsilon3 = ±1}
      Lambda(1/2 + u1 + epsilon2*u2 + epsilon3*u3)
    / product_j Lambda(1 + 2*uj).
```

Multiplying each external leg by its completed factor cancels the denominator.  This file uses the
canonical entire pole-filled version of the numerator, replacing each meromorphic `Lambda(s)` by
`xi(s) = s(s-1) Lambda(s)/2`, expressed through the corpus function `XiC`.  This changes only the
elementary factors at `0,1`; it preserves nontrivial divisor incidence.

The result is sharp and negative for RH selection.  The completed cubic vertex is invariant under
each Eisenstein Weyl reflection.  At every Xi divisor pole, and for every fixed physical continuum
leg, all but countably many partner frequencies give nonzero cubic coupling.  Thus the same vertex
lights the pole and its analytic shadow zero.  Angular EKG backreaction forces return-path mixing;

The squared continuum vertex is continuous and integrable by the actual theta/Xi horizontal decay.
The Weisskopf--Wigner boundary theorem then yields an exact finite-discrete plus continuum optical
energy identity, with strictly positive continuum rate at a bright channel.

`[LITERATURE]` Regularized triple-Eisenstein product: Zagier, *The Rankin--Selberg method for
automorphic functions which are not of rapid decay*; Michel--Venkatesh, PMIHES 111 (2010),
Section 4.5; Huang--Li, arXiv:2510.12322, Lemma 4.2.

`[PAPER-PROVED] [LEAN-PROVED] [HAWKING-SPECIFIC] [NO-GO]` This proves angular nonlinear incidence

/-- Entire pole-filled version of one completed-zeta factor `xi(1/2 + u)`. -/
def thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor (u : ℂ) : ℂ := XiC (-Complex.I * u)

/-- The completed factor is invariant under the Eisenstein Weyl reflection `u -> -u`. -/
theorem thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor_neg (u : ℂ) :
    thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor (-u) =
      thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor u := by
  unfold thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor
  have harg : -Complex.I * -u = -(-Complex.I * u) := by ring
  rw [harg, XiC_even]

/-- Entire numerator of the regularized triple-Eisenstein angular vertex. -/
def thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinCubicVertex (u₁ u₂ u₃ : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor (u₁ + u₂ + u₃) *
    thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor (u₁ - u₂ + u₃) *
    thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor (u₁ + u₂ - u₃) *
    thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor (u₁ - u₂ - u₃)

/-- Weyl reflection of first Eisenstein leg preserves completed vertex. -/
theorem thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinCubicVertex_neg_one (u₁ u₂ u₃ : ℂ) :
    thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinCubicVertex (-u₁) u₂ u₃ =
      thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinCubicVertex u₁ u₂ u₃ := by
  have h1 : thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor (-u₁ + u₂ + u₃) = thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor (u₁ - u₂ - u₃) := by
    rw [show -u₁ + u₂ + u₃ = -(u₁ - u₂ - u₃) by ring, thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor_neg]
  have h2 : thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor (-u₁ - u₂ + u₃) = thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor (u₁ + u₂ - u₃) := by
    rw [show -u₁ - u₂ + u₃ = -(u₁ + u₂ - u₃) by ring, thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor_neg]
  have h3 : thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor (-u₁ + u₂ - u₃) = thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor (u₁ - u₂ + u₃) := by
    rw [show -u₁ + u₂ - u₃ = -(u₁ - u₂ + u₃) by ring, thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor_neg]
  have h4 : thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor (-u₁ - u₂ - u₃) = thetaCuspHawkingCompletedEisensteinXiFactor (u₁ + u₂ + u₃) := by

/-!
# Monoid with zero and group with zero homomorphisms

This file defines homomorphisms of monoids with zero.

We also define coercion to a function, and usual operations: composition, identity homomorphism,
pointwise multiplication and pointwise inversion.


## Notation

* `→*₀`: `MonoidWithZeroHom`, the type of bundled `MonoidWithZero` homs. Also use for
  `GroupWithZero` homs.

## Implementation notes

Implicit `{}` brackets are often used instead of type class `[]` brackets.  This is done when the
instances can be inferred because they are implicit arguments to the type `MonoidHom`.  When they
can be inferred from the type it is faster to use this method than to use type class inference.

## Tags

monoid homomorphism
-/

@[expose] public section

assert_not_exists DenselyOrdered Ring

open Function

namespace NeZero
variable {F α β : Type*} [Zero α] [Zero β] [FunLike F α β] [ZeroHomClass F α β] {a : α}

lemma of_map (f : F) [neZero : NeZero (f a)] : NeZero a :=
  ⟨fun h ↦ ne (f a) <| by rw [h]; exact ZeroHomClass.map_zero f⟩

lemma of_injective {f : F} (hf : Injective f) [NeZero a] : NeZero (f a) :=
  ⟨by rw [← ZeroHomClass.map_zero f]; exact hf.ne NeZero.out⟩

end NeZero

variable {F α β γ δ M₀ : Type*} [MulZeroOneClass α] [MulZeroOneClass β] [MulZeroOneClass γ]
  [MulZeroOneClass δ]

/-- `MonoidWithZeroHomClass F α β` states that `F` is a type of
`MonoidWithZero`-preserving homomorphisms.

You should also extend this typeclass when you extend `MonoidWithZeroHom`. -/
class MonoidWithZeroHomClass (F : Type*) (α β : outParam Type*) [MulZeroOneClass α]
    [MulZeroOneClass β] [FunLike F α β] : Prop
  extends MonoidHomClass F α β, ZeroHomClass F α β

/-- `α →*₀ β` is the type of functions `α → β` that preserve
the `MonoidWithZero` structure.

`MonoidWithZeroHom` is also used for group homomorphisms.

When possible, instead of parametrizing results over `(f : α →*₀ β)`,
you should parametrize over `(F : Type*) [MonoidWithZeroHomClass F α β] (f : F)`.

When you extend this structure, make sure to extend `MonoidWithZeroHomClass`. -/
structure MonoidWithZeroHom (α β : Type*) [MulZeroOneClass α] [MulZeroOneClass β]
  extends ZeroHom α β, MonoidHom α β

/-- `α →*₀ β` denotes the type of zero-preserving monoid homomorphisms from `α` to `β`. -/
infixr:25 " →*₀ " => MonoidWithZeroHom

/-- Turn an element of a type `F` satisfying `MonoidWithZeroHomClass F α β` into an actual
`MonoidWithZeroHom`. -/
def MonoidWithZeroHom.ofClass [FunLike F α β] [MonoidWithZeroHomClass F α β]
    (f : F) : α →*₀ β := { (f : α →* β), (f : ZeroHom α β) with }

namespace MonoidWithZeroHom

attribute [nolint docBlame] toMonoidHom
attribute [nolint docBlame] toZeroHom

instance funLike : FunLike (α →*₀ β) α β where
  coe f := f.toFun
  coe_injective f g h := by obtain ⟨⟨_, _⟩, _⟩ := f; obtain ⟨⟨_, _⟩, _⟩ := g; congr

instance monoidWithZeroHomClass : MonoidWithZeroHomClass (α →*₀ β) α β where
  map_mul := MonoidWithZeroHom.map_mul'
  map_one := MonoidWithZeroHom.map_one'
  map_zero f := f.map_zero'

instance [Subsingleton α] : Subsingleton (α →*₀ β) := .of_oneHomClass

variable [FunLike F α β]

@[simp] lemma coe_ofClass [MonoidWithZeroHomClass F α β] (f : F) :
    (MonoidWithZeroHom.ofClass f : α → β) = f := rfl

-- Completely uninteresting lemmas about coercion to function, that all homs need
section Coes

/-! Bundled morphisms can be down-cast to weaker bundlings -/

attribute [coe] toMonoidHom

/-- `MonoidWithZeroHom` down-cast to a `MonoidHom`, forgetting the 0-preserving property. -/
instance coeToMonoidHom : Coe (α →*₀ β) (α →* β) :=

attribute [coe] toZeroHom

/-- `MonoidWithZeroHom` down-cast to a `ZeroHom`, forgetting the monoidal property. -/
instance coeToZeroHom : Coe (α →*₀ β) (ZeroHom α β) := ⟨toZeroHom⟩

-- This must come after the coe_toFun definitions
initialize_simps_projections MonoidWithZeroHom (toFun → apply)

@[simp] lemma coe_mk (f h1 hmul) : (mk f h1 hmul : α → β) = (f : α → β) := rfl

@[simp] lemma toZeroHom_coe (f : α →*₀ β) : (f.toZeroHom : α → β) = f := rfl

lemma toMonoidHom_coe (f : α →*₀ β) : f.toMonoidHom.toFun = f := rfl

@[ext] lemma ext ⦃f g : α →*₀ β⦄ (h : ∀ x, f x = g x) : f = g := DFunLike.ext _ _ h

@[simp] lemma mk_coe (f : α →*₀ β) (h1 hmul) : mk f h1 hmul = f := ext fun _ ↦ rfl

end Coes

/-- Copy of a `MonoidHom` with a new `toFun` equal to the old one. Useful to fix
definitional equalities. -/
protected def copy (f : α →*₀ β) (f' : α → β) (h : f' = f) : α →* β :=
  { f.toZeroHom.copy f' h, f.toMonoidHom.copy f' h with }

@[simp]
lemma coe_copy (f : α →*₀ β) (f' : α → β) (h) : (f.copy f' h) = f' := rfl

lemma copy_eq (f : α →*₀ β) (f' : α → β) (h) : f.copy f' h = f := DFunLike.ext' h

/-!
# The coefficient data of a normalized family

A finite family presented by shapes and limits, normalized by one member, produces exactly the data
the recurrence collapse consumes: the normalizing member is eventually nonzero, its own ratio is
`1`, and every ratio converges to an explicit constant — zero on the strictly dominated members.
-/

open Filter Topology Complex

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

/-- A function with a nonzero normalized limit is eventually nonzero. -/
theorem eventually_ne_zero_of_normalized {F shape : ℝ → ℂ} {c : ℂ} (hc : c ≠ 0)
    (hF : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => F t / shape t) atTop (nhds c)) :
    ∀ᶠ t : ℝ in atTop, F t ≠ 0 := by
  filter_upwards [hF.eventually_ne hc] with t ht
  intro h
  rw [h, zero_div] at ht
  exact ht rfl

/-- **The normalized family data.**  Normalizing a family by one member whose limit is nonzero: the
member is eventually nonzero, its shape ratio is `1`, and every ratio converges. -/
theorem tendsto_family_ratio_of_normalized {ι : Type*} {F shape : ι → ℝ → ℂ} {c r : ι → ℂ}
    (β : ι) (hcβ : c β ≠ 0) (hs : ∀ α, ∀ᶠ t : ℝ in atTop, shape α t ≠ 0)
    (hF : ∀ α, Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => F α t / shape α t) atTop (nhds (c α)))
    (hr : ∀ α, Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => shape α t / shape β t) atTop (nhds (r α))) :
    (∀ᶠ t : ℝ in atTop, F β t ≠ 0) ∧ r β = 1
      ∧ ∀ α, Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => F α t / F β t) atTop (nhds (c α * r α / c β)) := by
  have hone : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ => shape β t / shape β t) atTop (nhds 1) := by
    refine tendsto_const_nhds.congr' ?_
    filter_upwards [hs β] with t ht
    rw [div_self ht]
  have hrβ : r β = 1 := tendsto_nhds_unique (hr β) hone
  refine ⟨eventually_ne_zero_of_normalized hcβ (hF β), hrβ, fun α => ?_⟩
  exact tendsto_ratio_of_normalized hcβ (hs α) (hs β) (hF α) (hF β) (hr α)

/-- The normalizing member has ratio `1`. -/
theorem self_ratio_eq_one {ι : Type*} {c r : ι → ℂ} (β : ι) (hcβ : c β ≠ 0) (hrβ : r β = 1) :
    c β * r β / c β = 1 := by
  rw [hrβ, mul_one, div_self hcβ]

end GaloisForLFunctions

/-!
# Möbius-contact Gamma harmonic transverse-residue universality

The finite Möbius contact-charge defect is Gamma's exact reciprocal-factorial microscope scale.
Refining that charge by the harmonic pole parameter reveals the first nonzero direction beyond the
collapsed Riccati first-jet boundary. At each fixed pole the residue is contact charge times
digamma; its canonical pole-depth normalization tends to `-2`; and at every nonzero moving
microscope point the normalized defect tends to `-2/x`.
-/

open Complex Filter Topology

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- Möbius-contact factorial scale refined by the divergent harmonic pole parameter. -/
def mobiusContactGammaHarmonicMicroscopeScale (n : ℕ) : ℂ :=
  ((-2 - mobiusGammaContactPartialCharge n) / 2) * (harmonic n : ℂ)

/-- Contact-harmonic and intrinsic Gamma harmonic microscope scales coincide exactly. -/
theorem mobiusContactGammaHarmonicMicroscopeScale_eq (n : ℕ) :
    mobiusContactGammaHarmonicMicroscopeScale n =
      GaloisForLFunctions.gammaHarmonicMicroscopeScale n := by
  rw [mobiusContactGammaHarmonicMicroscopeScale,
    GaloisForLFunctions.gammaHarmonicMicroscopeScale,
    GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.mobiusContactGammaFactorialScale_eq]

/-- At pole `-n`, the exact transverse Riccati residue is the contact defect times the positive
integer digamma value. -/
theorem tendsto_gammaFactorialFirstJetDefect_mobiusContact_poleResidue
    (n : ℕ) :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℂ =>
        x * GaloisForLFunctions.gammaFactorialFirstJetDefect n x)
      (𝓝[≠] 0)
      (𝓝 (-2 * ((-2 - mobiusGammaContactPartialCharge n) / 2) *
        Complex.digamma ((n : ℂ) + 1))) := by
  simpa only [GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.mobiusContactGammaFactorialScale_eq] using
    (GaloisForLFunctions.tendsto_gammaFactorialFirstJetDefect_pole_residue n)

/-- Dividing fixed-pole residues by the contact-harmonic scale leaves the universal nonzero
direction `-2`. -/
theorem tendsto_normalized_gammaFactorialFirstJetDefect_mobiusContact_poleResidue :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ =>
      (-2 * ((-2 - mobiusGammaContactPartialCharge n) / 2) *
        Complex.digamma ((n : ℂ) + 1)) /
          mobiusContactGammaHarmonicMicroscopeScale n)
      atTop (𝓝 (-2)) := by
  simpa only [GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.mobiusContactGammaFactorialScale_eq,
    mobiusContactGammaHarmonicMicroscopeScale_eq] using
    GaloisForLFunctions.tendsto_normalized_gammaFactorialFirstJetDefect_pole_residue

/-- At every nonzero moving microscope point, the contact-harmonic-normalized Riccati defect tends
to the universal reciprocal direction `-2/x`. -/
theorem tendsto_gammaFactorialFirstJetDefect_div_mobiusContactHarmonicScale
    {x : ℂ} (hx : x ≠ 0) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ =>
      GaloisForLFunctions.gammaFactorialFirstJetDefect n x /
        mobiusContactGammaHarmonicMicroscopeScale n)
      atTop (𝓝 (-2 / x)) := by
  simpa only [mobiusContactGammaHarmonicMicroscopeScale_eq] using
    (GaloisForLFunctions.tendsto_gammaFactorialFirstJetDefect_div_harmonicScale hx)

/-- **Möbius-contact Gamma harmonic transverse-residue universality law.** The same arithmetic
contact defect controls exact local pole residue, canonical global pole-depth normalization, and
the full nonzero moving-microscope transverse profile. -/
theorem mobiusContactGammaHarmonic_completeTransverseResidueUniversality :
    (∀ n : ℕ,
      Tendsto (fun x : ℂ =>
          x * GaloisForLFunctions.gammaFactorialFirstJetDefect n x)
        (𝓝[≠] 0)
        (𝓝 (-2 * ((-2 - mobiusGammaContactPartialCharge n) / 2) *
          Complex.digamma ((n : ℂ) + 1)))) ∧
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ =>
      (-2 * ((-2 - mobiusGammaContactPartialCharge n) / 2) *
        Complex.digamma ((n : ℂ) + 1)) /
          mobiusContactGammaHarmonicMicroscopeScale n)
      atTop (𝓝 (-2)) ∧
    ∀ x : ℂ, x ≠ 0 →
      Tendsto (fun n : ℕ =>
        GaloisForLFunctions.gammaFactorialFirstJetDefect n x /
          mobiusContactGammaHarmonicMicroscopeScale n)
        atTop (𝓝 (-2 / x)) := by
  exact ⟨tendsto_gammaFactorialFirstJetDefect_mobiusContact_poleResidue,
    tendsto_normalized_gammaFactorialFirstJetDefect_mobiusContact_poleResidue,
    fun x hx =>
      tendsto_gammaFactorialFirstJetDefect_div_mobiusContactHarmonicScale hx⟩

end

testAgainstNN f := by
  nth_rw 1 [μ.self_eq_mass_smul_normalize]
  rw [μ.normalize.toFiniteMeasure.smul_testAgainstNN_apply μ.mass f, smul_eq_mul]

theorem normalize_testAgainstNN (nonzero : μ ≠ 0) (f : Ω →ᵇ ℝ≥0) :
    μ.normalize.toFiniteMeasure.testAgainstNN f = μ.mass⁻¹ * μ.testAgainstNN f := by
  simp [μ.testAgainstNN_eq_mass_mul, inv_mul_cancel_left₀ <| μ.mass_nonzero_iff.mpr nonzero]

variable [OpensMeasurableSpace Ω]
variable {μ}

theorem tendsto_testAgainstNN_of_tendsto_normalize_testAgainstNN_of_tendsto_mass {γ : Type*}
    {F : Filter γ} {μs : γ → FiniteMeasure Ω}
    (μs_lim : Tendsto (fun i ↦ (μs i).normalize) F (𝓝 μ.normalize))
    (mass_lim : Tendsto (fun i ↦ (μs i).mass) F (𝓝 μ.mass)) (f : Ω →ᵇ ℝ≥0) :
    Tendsto (fun i ↦ (μs i).testAgainstNN f) F (𝓝 (μ.testAgainstNN f)) := by
  by_cases h_mass : μ.mass = 0
  · simp only [μ.mass_zero_iff.mp h_mass, zero_testAgainstNN_apply, zero_mass] at mass_lim ⊢
    exact tendsto_zero_testAgainstNN_of_tendsto_zero_mass mass_lim f
  simp_rw [fun i ↦ (μs i).testAgainstNN_eq_mass_mul f, μ.testAgainstNN_eq_mass_mul f]
  rw [ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_nhds_iff_toFiniteMeasure_tendsto_nhds] at μs_lim
  rw [tendsto_iff_forall_testAgainstNN_tendsto] at μs_lim
  have lim_pair :
    Tendsto (fun i ↦ (⟨(μs i).mass, (μs i).normalize.toFiniteMeasure.testAgainstNN f⟩ : ℝ≥0 × ℝ≥0))
      F (𝓝 ⟨μ.mass, μ.normalize.toFiniteMeasure.testAgainstNN f⟩) :=
    (Prod.tendsto_iff _ _).mpr ⟨mass_lim, μs_lim f⟩
  exact tendsto_mul.comp lim_pair

theorem tendsto_normalize_testAgainstNN_of_tendsto {γ : Type*} {F : Filter γ}
    {μs : γ → FiniteMeasure Ω} (μs_lim : Tendsto μs F (𝓝 μ)) (nonzero : μ ≠ 0) (f : Ω →ᵇ ℝ≥0) :
    Tendsto (fun i ↦ (μs i).normalize.toFiniteMeasure.testAgainstNN f) F
      (𝓝 (μ.normalize.toFiniteMeasure.testAgainstNN f)) := by
  have lim_mass := μs_lim.mass
  have aux : {(0 : ℝ≥0)}ᶜ ∈ 𝓝 μ.mass :=
    isOpen_compl_singleton.mem_nhds (μ.mass_nonzero_iff.mpr nonzero)
  have eventually_nonzero : ∀ᶠ i in F, μs i ≠ 0 := by
    simp_rw [← mass_nonzero_iff]
    exact lim_mass aux
  have eve : ∀ᶠ i in F,
      (μs i).normalize.toFiniteMeasure.testAgainstNN f =
        (μs i).mass⁻¹ * (μs i).testAgainstNN f := by
    filter_upwards [eventually_iff.mp eventually_nonzero]
    intro i hi
    apply normalize_testAgainstNN _ hi
  simp_rw [tendsto_congr' eve, μ.normalize_testAgainstNN nonzero]
  have lim_pair :
    Tendsto (fun i ↦ (⟨(μs i).mass⁻¹, (μs i).testAgainstNN f⟩ : ℝ≥0 × ℝ≥0)) F
      (𝓝 ⟨μ.mass⁻¹, μ.testAgainstNN f⟩) := by
    refine (Prod.tendsto_iff _ _).mpr ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · exact (continuousOn_inv₀.continuousAt aux).tendsto.comp lim_mass
    · exact tendsto_iff_forall_testAgainstNN_tendsto.mp μs_lim f
  exact tendsto_mul.comp lim_pair

/-- If the normalized versions of finite measures converge weakly and their total masses
also converge, then the finite measures themselves converge weakly. -/
theorem tendsto_of_tendsto_normalize_testAgainstNN_of_tendsto_mass {γ : Type*} {F : Filter γ}
    {μs : γ → FiniteMeasure Ω} (μs_lim : Tendsto (fun i ↦ (μs i).normalize) F (𝓝 μ.normalize))
    (mass_lim : Tendsto (fun i ↦ (μs i).mass) F (𝓝 μ.mass)) : Tendsto μs F (𝓝 μ) := by
  rw [tendsto_iff_forall_testAgainstNN_tendsto]
  exact fun f ↦
    tendsto_testAgainstNN_of_tendsto_normalize_testAgainstNN_of_tendsto_mass μs_lim mass_lim f

/-- If finite measures themselves converge weakly to a nonzero limit measure, then their
normalized versions also converge weakly. -/
theorem tendsto_normalize_of_tendsto {γ : Type*} {F : Filter γ} {μs : γ → FiniteMeasure Ω}
    (μs_lim : Tendsto μs F (𝓝 μ)) (nonzero : μ ≠ 0) :
    Tendsto (fun i ↦ (μs i).normalize) F (𝓝 μ.normalize) := by
  rw [ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_nhds_iff_toFiniteMeasure_tendsto_nhds,
    tendsto_iff_forall_testAgainstNN_tendsto]
  exact fun f ↦ tendsto_normalize_testAgainstNN_of_tendsto μs_lim nonzero f

/-- The weak convergence of finite measures to a nonzero limit can be characterized by the weak
convergence of both their normalized versions (probability measures) and their total masses. -/
theorem tendsto_normalize_iff_tendsto {γ : Type*} {F : Filter γ} {μs : γ → FiniteMeasure Ω}
    (nonzero : μ ≠ 0) :
    Tendsto (fun i ↦ (μs i).normalize) F (𝓝 μ.normalize) ∧
        Tendsto (fun i ↦ (μs i).mass) F (𝓝 μ.mass) ↔
      Tendsto μs F (𝓝 μ) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨normalized_lim, mass_lim⟩
    exact tendsto_of_tendsto_normalize_testAgainstNN_of_tendsto_mass normalized_lim mass_lim
  · intro μs_lim
    exact ⟨tendsto_normalize_of_tendsto μs_lim nonzero, μs_lim.mass⟩

# Leading-symbol degeneracy magnitude-survival universality law

## Status

In progress — paper proof and exact Lean source check complete; literature novelty audit pending.

## Theorem-first provenance

- `HTGeometry/WeightPolynomialDependence.lean`
  - `weightPolynomial_class44_dependence`
- `HTGeometry/LogSuperlacunaryMagnitudeHypertranscendence.lean`
  - `hypertranscendental_of_eventually_logSuperlacunary`
- `HTGeometry/MagnitudeDistinctSurvival.lean`
  - theorem surface documenting minimal-valuation survival without a leading-symbol hypothesis

## Universal law

The explicit degree-four, order-four differential polynomial

`Y₃Y₁Y₀² - 2Y₂²Y₀² + Y₂Y₁²Y₀`

is nonzero, but its balanced falling-factorial leading symbol vanishes identically.  Nevertheless it
cannot annihilate any entire function whose Taylor magnitudes are eventually positive and
log-superlacunary.

Thus balanced leading-symbol nondegeneracy is sufficient but not necessary for magnitude survival:
minimal-valuation dominance detects a universal family of relations lying in the exact blind spot
of the balanced-symbol method.

## Paper proof

The existing class-`(4,4)` falling-factorial identity proves that the balanced leading symbol is
zero.  The differential polynomial itself is nonzero: evaluating the value, first derivative, and
third derivative variables at one and the second derivative variable at zero gives one.  Eventual
log-superlacunary Taylor magnitudes force hypertranscendence, so no nonzero polynomial in the point,
value, and finitely many derivatives can vanish identically.  Applying this to the explicit
third-order polynomial proves survival despite exact symbol cancellation.

# The simple-pole jet lattice has an exact holographic selection law

- **ID:** `simple-pole-jet-lattice-holographic-selection-law`
- **Stage:** 1-in-progress
- **Type:** THEOREM (universal/profile parts) / CONJECTURE (native global Gamma intersection) / HT BOUNDARY-GEOMETRY CANDIDATE
- **Scientific status:** `[PROVED AND FORMALIZED: UNIVERSAL LAW, CONSTANT-COEFFICIENT HORIZON, C(n)-RELATIVE SCALE/DERIVATIVE FREEDOM, MOVING C[z] TAYLOR REFLECTION, FAITHFUL TWO-STAGE LAURENT PROFILE, CONSERVED TRI-GRADING, NONLINEAR MAXIMAL-WEIGHT REFLECTION, FULL SYMBOLIC/ACTUAL MOVING-POLE JET INJECTIVITY, EXACT MOVING-COEFFICIENT AFFINE PROFILE HORIZON, DYNAMIC COVARIANT GAMMA VALUE REALIZATION, AND FIRST/SECOND-SUBPRINCIPAL REFLECTION] [OPEN: NATIVE MEROMORPHIC-ORDER TO FROZEN-PROFILE DESCENT] [GLOBAL GAMMA INTERSECTION IS A CANDIDATE, NOT YET A THEOREM] [NOVELTY UNVERIFIED]`
- **Methods:** symbolic proof and Lean verification only; no numerical computation

## Constraint

Let a simple-pole germ be written

```text
f(t)=U(t)/t,
```

where `U` is regular and `U(0)` is nonzero.  Give pole order, rather than the ordinary Laurent
exponent, positive sign.  Leibniz gives the exact finite pole profile

```text
f^(j)(t)
  = sum_(k=0)^j binom(j,k) U^(k)(t) (-1)^(j-k) (j-k)! t^(-(j-k+1)).       (1)
```

Introduce a pole-grade variable `T` and independent boundary-jet variables `X_k`.  Equation `(1)`
defines

```text
J_j(T)=sum_(k=0)^j binom(j,k)(-1)^(j-k)(j-k)! X_k T^(j-k+1).              (2)
```

For a constant-coefficient differential polynomial `P(Y_0,Y_1,...)`, its simple-pole profile is

```text
H(P)=P(J_0,J_1,...).                                                       (3)
```

This is a static valuation constraint.  It introduces no time evolution or generative flow.

## Theorem A: exact particle-number boundary trace `[PROVED HERE]`

Suppose `P` is homogeneous of total differential degree `d`.  Then

```text
[T^d] H(P)=P(X_0,X_1,...).                                                 (4)
```

Consequently, if `P` is nonzero, its pole-grade-`d` boundary trace is nonzero.  After specializing
the `X_k` to any algebraically independent family, the trace remains nonzero.

### Proof

Every `J_j` has a common factor `T`:

```text
J_j(T)=T R_j(T),       R_j(0)=X_j.                                        (5)
```

Homogeneity gives

```text
H(P)=T^d P(R_0,R_1,...).                                                    (6)
```

Taking the coefficient of `T^d` is the same as setting every `R_j` to its constant term.  By
`(5)` this gives `P(X_0,X_1,...)`, proving `(4)`.  Algebraic independence makes evaluation on the
actual boundary family injective.

## Theorem B: the universal simple-pole horizon is affine `[PROVED HERE]`

Assume the boundary variables are algebraically free and `X_0` is nonzero.  Then

```text
H(C[Y_0,Y_1,...]) intersect C[X_0,X_1,...][T]_(degree <= 1)

P_1=sum_(j=0)^r c_j Y_j,
```

and take the largest `J` with `c_J` nonzero.  The coefficient of `T^(J+1)` in `H(P_1)` is

```text
c_J (-1)^J J! X_0,
```

which is nonzero.  At-most-simple pole grade therefore forces `J=0`.  This leaves exactly
`C+C Y_0`, proving `(7)`.

# Finite-Order Local Frequency Operators Are Not Markov

- **ID:** finite-order-local-frequency-operators-not-markov
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper) / source-transfer guardrail
- **Grade:** BRIDGE / guardrail. Door-2 reduces the proof to eventual sign of a
  real polynomial, so this is not a native theorem. Its role is to exclude a
  false completed-interaction shape.
- **Source:** `../../3-formalized/not_new_scientific_knowledge/positive-even-frequency-cone-not-markov.md`;
  `../../3-formalized/not_new_scientific_knowledge/finite-signed-even-frequency-atoms-not-markov.md`;
  `source-selector-repair-obligation-ledger.md`
- **Statement:** Applying any nonzero finite-order coefficient-local operator
  with real polynomial degree-symbol to a nonzero positive FE-even frequency
  mixture still cannot produce a Markov/Stieltjes moment sequence in the
  seam-square coordinate.

## Setup

Let `mu` be a nonzero positive Borel measure on `(0,infty)` such that all even
moments are finite. Define

`L_mu(z)=int_0^infty (cosh(lambda sqrt(z))-1) dmu(lambda)`.

Thus

`[z^k]L_mu(z)=(int lambda^(2k)dmu(lambda))/(2k)!`, for `k>=1`.

Let `q in R[X]` be a nonzero real polynomial. Think of `q` as the degree-symbol
of a finite-order local operator in the Euler operator `D=z d/dz`: on a power
series, `q(D)` multiplies the `z^k` coefficient by `q(k)`.

Define the transformed shifted seam moments

`T_k^{q,mu}=-2k(-1)^k q(k)[z^k]L_mu(z)`.

Equivalently,

`T_k^{q,mu}=(-1)^(k+1) q(k) (int lambda^(2k)dmu(lambda))/(2k-1)!`.

## Theorem

If `q` is nonzero and `mu` is nonzero positive, then `T_k^{q,mu}<0` for
infinitely many `k`.

Consequently `(T_k^{q,mu})_{k>=1}` is not the moment sequence of a positive
Borel measure on `R_+`.

## Proof

For every `k>=1`, positivity and nonzero support on `(0,infty)` give

`M_k=int lambda^(2k)dmu(lambda)>0`.

A nonzero real polynomial has only finitely many real roots and has a constant
sign for all sufficiently large real arguments. Hence there is `K` and a sign
`eps in {+1,-1}` such that

`eps q(k)>0`

for every integer `k>=K`.

For those `k`,

`sign(T_k^{q,mu}) = (-1)^(k+1) eps`,

because `M_k/(2k-1)!` is strictly positive. Therefore one tail parity has
negative transformed shifted moments:

- if `eps=+1`, every sufficiently large even `k` has `T_k^{q,mu}<0`;
- if `eps=-1`, every sufficiently large odd `k` has `T_k^{q,mu}<0`.

A positive measure on `R_+` has nonnegative moments. Thus no positive
Markov/Stieltjes representation exists.

## Consequence For Local Completed-Correction Routes

`../../3-formalized/not_new_scientific_knowledge/positive-even-frequency-cone-not-markov.md` kills direct positive summation over
FE-even frequencies. `../../3-formalized/not_new_scientific_knowledge/finite-signed-even-frequency-atoms-not-markov.md` kills a
finite signed real-atom patch. This theorem kills a different escape: applying a
finite-order local operator whose coefficient action is polynomial in the degree.

The obstruction is parity, not scale. Polynomial degree multipliers can change
amplitude and finite initial data, but they cannot supply the alternating factor
needed to move a positive FE-even frequency source into the Markov cone.

Therefore a source proof of seam-log Markov positivity cannot be a finite-order
local correction of the positive frequency source. It must use an all-order or
nonlocal completed interaction, a multiplicative correlation identity, or a
closed boundary/index construction.

## Boundary

This theorem does not rule out infinite-order operators, operators with
non-polynomial degree-symbol carrying an explicit parity factor, nonlocal
transforms, complex/imaginary frequencies, or the completed explicit formula.
Those are precisely the mechanisms still outside this finite-local obstruction.

## Theatre Test

For any proposed completed-correction proof:

1. Does the correction act coefficientwise as multiplication by a real
   polynomial `q(k)`?
2. Is the source being corrected a nonzero positive FE-even real-frequency
   mixture?
3. If yes, `q(k)` has a tail sign and the FE parity forces negative moments on
   one tail parity.
4. Which line of the proof uses an all-order/nonlocal mechanism that escapes a
   polynomial degree-symbol?

The proof is elementary. The significance is route-local: it prevents a finite
local differential or finite-part multiplier from being presented as the
completed interaction needed by the seam-log Markov target.

/-- Run each registered `positivity` extension on an expression, returning a `NormNum.Result`. -/
def core (pα? : Option Q(PartialOrder $α)) (e : Q($α)) : MetaM (Strictness zα e pα?) := do
  let mut result := .none
  trace[Tactic.positivity] "trying to prove positivity of {e}"
  for ext in ← (positivityExt.getState (← getEnv)).2.getMatch e do
    try
      result ← orElse result <| ext.eval zα pα? e
    catch err =>
      trace[Tactic.positivity] "{e} failed: {err.toMessageData}"
  trace[Tactic.positivity] "current result from positivity extensions: {result.toString}"
  match h : pα?, result with
  | some pα, res =>
    trace[Tactic.positivity] "{α} has some {pα}"
    let mut res ← orElse res <| normNumPositivity zα pα e
    trace[Tactic.positivity] "current result from normNum: {res.toString}"
    res ← orElse res <| positivityCanon zα pα e
    trace[Tactic.positivity] "current result from canonicity: {res.toString}"
    if let .positive _ := res then
      trace[Tactic.positivity] "{e} => {res.toString}"
      return h ▸ res
    for ldecl in ← getLCtx do
      if !ldecl.isImplementationDetail then
        res ← orElse res <| compareHyp zα pα e ldecl
    trace[Tactic.positivity] "{e} => {res.toString}"
    throwNone (pure (h ▸ res))
  | .none, _ =>
    trace[Tactic.positivity] "{α} has no PartialOrder"
    if let .nonzero _ := result then
      trace[Tactic.positivity] "{e} => {result.toString}"
      return result
    for ldecl in ← getLCtx do
      if !ldecl.isImplementationDetail then
        result ← orElse result <| compareHypNonzero zα e ldecl
    trace[Tactic.positivity] "{e} => {result.toString}"
    throwNone (pure result)


private inductive OrderRel : Type
| le : OrderRel -- `0 ≤ a`
| lt : OrderRel -- `0 < a`
| ne : OrderRel -- `a ≠ 0`
| ne' : OrderRel -- `0 ≠ a`

end Meta.Positivity
namespace Meta.Positivity

/-- Given an expression `e`, use the core method of the `positivity` tactic to prove it positive,
or, failing that, nonnegative; return a Boolean (signalling whether the strict or non-strict
inequality was established) together with the proof as an expression. -/
def bestResult (e : Expr) : MetaM (Bool × Expr) := do
  let ⟨u, α, _⟩ ← inferTypeQ' e
  let zα ← synthInstanceQ q(Zero $α)
  let pα? ← try? <| synthInstanceQ q(PartialOrder $α)
  assumeInstancesCommute
  match pα?, ← try? (Meta.Positivity.core zα pα? e) with
  | _, some (.positive pf) => pure (true, pf)
  | _, some (.nonnegative pf) => pure (false, pf)
  | _, _ => throwError "could not establish the nonnegativity of {e}"

/-- Given an expression `e`, use the core method of the `positivity` tactic to prove it nonnegative.
-/
def proveNonneg (e : Expr) : MetaM Expr := do
  let (strict, pf) ← bestResult e
  if strict then mkAppM ``le_of_lt #[pf] else pure pf

/-- An auxiliary entry point to the `positivity` tactic. Given a proposition `t` of the form
`0 [≤/</≠] e`, attempts to recurse on the structure of `t` to prove it. It returns a proof
or fails. -/
def solve (t : Q(Prop)) : MetaM Expr := do
  let rest {u : Level} (α : Q(Type u)) z e (relDesired : OrderRel) : MetaM Expr := do
    let zα ← synthInstanceQ q(Zero $α)
    let .true ← isDefEq z q(0 : $α) | throwError "not a positivity goal"
    let pα? ← try? <| synthInstanceQ q(PartialOrder $α)
    let r ← catchNone <| Meta.Positivity.core zα pα? e
    let throw (a b : String) : MetaM Expr := throwError
      "failed to prove {a}, but it would be possible to prove {b} if desired"
    match (dependent := true) pα? with
    | some _ =>
      match relDesired, r with
      | .lt, .positive p
      | .le, .nonnegative p
      | .ne, .nonzero p => pure p
      | .le, .positive p => pure q(le_of_lt $p)
      | .ne, .positive p => pure q(ne_of_gt $p)
      | .ne', .positive p => pure q(ne_of_lt $p)
      | .ne', .nonzero p => pure q(Ne.symm $p)
      | .lt, .nonnegative _ => throw "strict positivity" "nonnegativity"
      | .lt, .nonzero _ => throw "strict positivity" "nonzeroness"
      | .le, .nonzero _ => throw "nonnegativity" "nonzeroness"
      | .ne, .nonnegative _
      | .ne', .nonnegative _ => throw "nonzeroness" "nonnegativity"
      | _, .none => throwError "failed to prove positivity/nonnegativity/nonzeroness"
    | none =>
      match relDesired, r with
      | .ne, .nonzero p => pure p
      | .ne', .nonzero p => pure q(Ne.symm $p)
      | .lt, .nonzero _ => throw "strict positivity" "nonzeroness"
      | .le, .nonzero _ => throw "nonnegativity" "nonzeroness"
      | _, _ => throwError "failed to prove nonzeroness"
  match t with
  | ~q(@LE.le $α $_a $z $e) => rest α z e .le
  | ~q(@LT.lt $α $_a $z $e) => rest α z e .lt
  | ~q($a ≠ ($b : ($α : Type _))) =>
    let _zα ← synthInstanceQ q(Zero $α)
    if ← isDefEq b q((0 : $α)) then
      rest α b a .ne
    else
      let .true ← isDefEq a q((0 : $α)) | throwError "not a positivity goal"
      rest α a b .ne'
  | _ => throwError "not a positivity goal"

/-
# The exponential-period corank: reducing Stieltjes irrationality to integer linear forms

The archimedean regularization constants of `ζ` at its pole `s = 1` — the Stieltjes constants, of
which `γ₀ = eulerMascheroniConstant` is the first — are the "non-period" side of the seam
`ξ = (Γ-factor)·ζ`: conjecturally exponential periods, independent of the period algebra of the
convergent `ζ`-values `{ζ(k)}_{k≥2} = {(1/j!)·∫₀^∞ tʲ/(eᵗ−1)\,dt}`. The apex question (does the
non-period side escape the period field) rests, at its weakest necessary point, on the irrationality
of `eulerMascheroniConstant`.

This file formalizes the **mechanism** by which such irrationality/independence is decided — the
integer-linear-forms criterion (the engine behind Rivoal–Ball / Nesterenko / Apéry) — and thereby
reduces the open atom to an explicit *construction* problem:

* `irrational_of_linearForms` — if integer forms `pₙ + qₙ·α` are nonzero and tend to `0`, then `α`
  is irrational (a nonzero rational with bounded denominator is bounded away from `0`).
* `not_all_rat_of_linearForms` — the family version: nonzero integer forms `aₙ + Σᵢ bₙᵢ·xᵢ` tending
  to `0` force some `xᵢ` irrational (the form is a nonzero rational of denominator dividing the fixed
  product of the `xᵢ`-denominators, hence `≥ 1/D`).
* `eulerMascheroniConstant_irrational_of_linearForms` — the atom, localized: `γ₀` is irrational as
  soon as such integer forms exist.

The reason the construction resists (the analytic core of the open problem, not formalizable
unconditionally): the natural approximants `harmonic n − log n → γ₀` (`Real.tendsto_harmonic_sub_log`)
carry the transcendental `log n`, so they are *not* integer forms in `γ₀`; and the coefficient-
extraction forms `∮ (ζ(1+z) − 1/z) Q(z)\,dz` are dominated by the factorial `Γ`-factor of the
functional equation, obstructing the required smallness. Producing genuine integer forms in the
Stieltjes constants — defeating the `log`/`Γ` entanglement — is the irreducible open input; the
criterion below is the exact interface it must feed.
-/
import Mathlib

open Filter Topology

namespace GaloisForLFunctions

/-- **Integer-linear-forms irrationality criterion.**  If there are integer linear forms
`pₙ + qₙ·α` that are nonzero for every `n` and tend to `0`, then `α` is irrational.  Were `α = c`
rational, each form would be `mₙ / c.den` with `mₙ ∈ ℤ` nonzero, hence `|·| ≥ 1/c.den > 0`,
contradicting convergence to `0`.  This is the engine of the Rivoal–Ball/Nesterenko method. -/
theorem irrational_of_linearForms (α : ℝ) (p q : ℕ → ℤ)
    (hne : ∀ n, (p n : ℝ) + (q n : ℝ) * α ≠ 0)
    (h0 : Tendsto (fun n => (p n : ℝ) + (q n : ℝ) * α) atTop (𝓝 0)) :
    Irrational α := by
  rintro ⟨c, hc⟩
  set d : ℤ := (c.den : ℤ) with hd
  have hdpos : (0 : ℝ) < (d : ℝ) := by rw [hd]; exact_mod_cast c.pos
  have hαeq : α = (c.num : ℝ) / (d : ℝ) := by
    rw [← hc, hd]; push_cast [Rat.cast_def]; ring
  have key : ∀ n, (p n : ℝ) + (q n : ℝ) * α
      = ((p n * d + q n * c.num : ℤ) : ℝ) / (d : ℝ) := by
    intro n; rw [hαeq]; field_simp; push_cast; ring
  have hlb : ∀ n, (1 : ℝ) / (d : ℝ) ≤ |(p n : ℝ) + (q n : ℝ) * α| := by
    intro n
    have hmn : (p n * d + q n * c.num : ℤ) ≠ 0 := by
      intro hz; apply hne n; rw [key n, hz]; norm_num
    have h1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ |((p n * d + q n * c.num : ℤ) : ℝ)| := by
      rw [← Int.cast_abs]; exact_mod_cast Int.one_le_abs hmn
    rw [key n, abs_div, abs_of_pos hdpos]; gcongr
  have habs : Tendsto (fun n => |(p n : ℝ) + (q n : ℝ) * α|) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
    simpa using h0.abs
  obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ :=
    (habs.eventually (eventually_lt_nhds (by positivity : (0 : ℝ) < 1 / (d : ℝ)))).exists
  exact absurd (hlb n) (not_le.mpr hn)

/-- **Family linear-forms criterion.**  If there are integer linear forms `aₙ + Σᵢ bₙᵢ·xᵢ` in a
finite family `x : Fin k → ℝ`, nonzero for every `n` and tending to `0`, then the `xᵢ` are **not all
rational**.  Were every `xᵢ = rᵢ ∈ ℚ`, each form would be a rational of denominator dividing the fixed
`D = ∏ᵢ (rᵢ).den`, i.e. `mₙ / D` with `mₙ ∈ ℤ` nonzero, hence `|·| ≥ 1/D`, contradicting convergence
to `0`.  This is the joint (independence-flavored) form of the criterion, the shape a DSS-cross-style
attack on the whole Stieltjes family would feed. -/
theorem not_all_rat_of_linearForms {k : ℕ} (x : Fin k → ℝ) (a : ℕ → ℤ) (b : ℕ → Fin k → ℤ)
    (hne : ∀ n, (a n : ℝ) + ∑ i, (b n i : ℝ) * x i ≠ 0)
    (h0 : Tendsto (fun n => (a n : ℝ) + ∑ i, (b n i : ℝ) * x i) atTop (𝓝 0)) :
    ¬ ∀ i, ∃ r : ℚ, x i = (r : ℝ) := by
  rintro hrat
  choose r hr using hrat
  set D : ℤ := ∏ i, ((r i).den : ℤ) with hD
  have hDpos : (0 : ℝ) < (D : ℝ) := by
    rw [hD]; push_cast
    exact Finset.prod_pos fun i _ => by exact_mod_cast (r i).pos
  have hDr : ∀ i, ∃ z : ℤ, (r i : ℝ) * (D : ℝ) = (z : ℝ) := by
    intro i
    refine ⟨(r i).num * ∏ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, ((r j).den : ℤ), ?_⟩
    rw [hD, ← Finset.prod_erase_mul _ _ (Finset.mem_univ i)]
    push_cast [Rat.cast_def]; field_simp

/-!
# The small linear form and its perturbed normalization

Baker's method is run on a relation.  For the *effective* theorem the relation is not exact: one
assumes only that the form is small, and every use of the exact normalization

`log p_pivot = −Σ_{i≠pivot} (bᵢ/b_pivot) log pᵢ`

acquires the explicit error `Λ/b_pivot`.  This file fixes the object carrying that data — a nonzero
integer coefficient vector together with a pivot at which the coefficient is maximal in absolute
value — and proves the perturbed normalization, the elementary consequences of maximality, and the
comparison between the `ℓ¹` and `ℓ^∞` heights.

Choosing the pivot maximal is what makes the normalized coefficients bounded by one, which is the
form the auxiliary construction consumes.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Matveev

open Finset

variable {d : ℕ}

/-- The `ℓ^∞` height of an integer coefficient vector. -/
def coeffSup (ν : Fin d → ℤ) : ℕ := Finset.univ.sup (fun i => (ν i).natAbs)

theorem coeffSup_le_coeffHeight (ν : Fin d → ℤ) : coeffSup ν ≤ coeffHeight ν := by
  classical
  refine Finset.sup_le fun i _ => ?_
  rw [coeffHeight]
  exact Finset.single_le_sum (f := fun j => (ν j).natAbs) (fun j _ => Nat.zero_le _)
    (Finset.mem_univ i)

theorem coeffHeight_le_card_mul_coeffSup (ν : Fin d → ℤ) :
    coeffHeight ν ≤ d * coeffSup ν := by
  classical
  rw [coeffHeight]
  calc ∑ i, (ν i).natAbs ≤ ∑ _i : Fin d, coeffSup ν :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ =>
          Finset.le_sup (f := fun j => (ν j).natAbs) (Finset.mem_univ i)
    _ = d * coeffSup ν := by simp

theorem coeffSup_eq_zero_iff (ν : Fin d → ℤ) : coeffSup ν = 0 ↔ ν = 0 := by
  classical
  constructor
  · intro h
    funext i
    have hi : (ν i).natAbs ≤ coeffSup ν :=
      Finset.le_sup (f := fun j => (ν j).natAbs) (Finset.mem_univ i)
    rw [h] at hi
    show ν i = 0
    omega
  · intro h
    subst h
    simp [coeffSup]

/-- **A maximal pivot exists.**  Every nonzero coefficient vector has an index at which the absolute
value attains the `ℓ^∞` height. -/
theorem exists_max_pivot (ν : Fin d → ℤ) (hν : ν ≠ 0) :
    ∃ k : Fin d, ν k ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ i, (ν i).natAbs ≤ (ν k).natAbs := by
  classical
  have hne : (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin d)).Nonempty := by
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos d with hd | hd
    · exfalso
      apply hν
      funext i
      exact absurd i.2 (by omega)
    · exact Finset.univ_nonempty_iff.mpr (Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp hd)
  obtain ⟨k, _, hk⟩ := Finset.exists_max_image Finset.univ (fun i => (ν i).natAbs) hne
  refine ⟨k, ?_, fun i => hk i (Finset.mem_univ i)⟩
  intro hzero
  apply hν
  funext i
  have hi := hk i (Finset.mem_univ i)
  rw [hzero] at hi
  simp only [Int.natAbs_zero, Nat.le_zero] at hi
  show ν i = 0
  omega

/-! ## The small-form object -/

/-- A nonzero integer linear form in prime logarithms, with a distinguished pivot at which the
coefficient is maximal in absolute value. -/
structure SmallForm (d : ℕ) where
  /-- the prime family -/
  p : Fin d → ℕ
  /-- the primes are distinct -/
  p_injective : Function.Injective p
  /-- every entry is prime -/
  p_prime : ∀ i, (p i).Prime
  /-- the integer coefficient vector -/
  b : Fin d → ℤ
  /-- the coefficient vector is nonzero -/
  b_ne_zero : b ≠ 0
  /-- the pivot index -/
  pivot : Fin d
  /-- the pivot coefficient is nonzero -/
  pivot_ne_zero : b pivot ≠ 0
  /-- the pivot coefficient is maximal -/
  pivot_max : ∀ i, (b i).natAbs ≤ (b pivot).natAbs

namespace SmallForm

variable (S : SmallForm d)

/-- The value of the linear form. -/
def value : ℝ := primeLogForm S.p S.b

/-- The normalized coefficients, bounded by one in absolute value. -/
def normCoeff (i : Fin d) : ℝ := (S.b i : ℝ) / (S.b S.pivot : ℝ)

theorem pivot_cast_ne_zero : ((S.b S.pivot : ℤ) : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
  exact_mod_cast S.pivot_ne_zero

theorem abs_normCoeff_le_one (i : Fin d) : |S.normCoeff i| ≤ 1 := by
  have hpiv : (0 : ℝ) < |((S.b S.pivot : ℤ) : ℝ)| := abs_pos.mpr S.pivot_cast_ne_zero
  rw [normCoeff, abs_div, div_le_one hpiv]
  have hnat : (S.b i).natAbs ≤ (S.b S.pivot).natAbs := S.pivot_max i
  have hint : |S.b i| ≤ |S.b S.pivot| := by
    rw [Int.abs_eq_natAbs, Int.abs_eq_natAbs]
    exact_mod_cast hnat
  calc |((S.b i : ℤ) : ℝ)| = ((|S.b i| : ℤ) : ℝ) := by
        rw [← Int.cast_abs]
    _ ≤ ((|S.b S.pivot| : ℤ) : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hint
    _ = |((S.b S.pivot : ℤ) : ℝ)| := by rw [← Int.cast_abs]

theorem normCoeff_pivot : S.normCoeff S.pivot = 1 := by
  rw [normCoeff, div_self S.pivot_cast_ne_zero]

/-- **The perturbed normalization.**  Solving the small form for the pivot logarithm leaves the
exact error `Λ/b_pivot`; with an exactly vanishing form this is the classical normalization. -/
theorem pivot_log_eq :
    Real.log (S.p S.pivot)
      = -∑ i ∈ Finset.univ.erase S.pivot, S.normCoeff i * Real.log (S.p i)
        + S.value / (S.b S.pivot : ℝ) := by
  have hsplit : S.value

/-!
# Beta-sensitivity and arithmetic evaluability are mutually exclusive

The classification asks for a weight that separates `β = 1/2` from `β = 1/2 + a`.  In its exact form
that means a function vanishing **precisely** on the critical line.  This file shows no analytic
function can do that, and draws the consequence.

**The obstruction.**  The zero set of a nonzero analytic function on a connected domain is discrete;
the line `Re s = 1/2` is not.  So a function vanishing on the whole line vanishes identically.  Any
weight that detects the critical line exactly is therefore **non-analytic** — for instance
`ρ ↦ |φ(ρ) - φ(1 - ρ̄)|`, whose modulus and conjugation are both non-analytic, and which vanishes on
the line for every choice of `φ`.

**The consequence.**  The explicit formula evaluates `Σ_ρ h(ρ)` by contour shifting, which requires
`h` analytic.  A non-analytic weight has no such evaluation: it cannot be expressed through the primes
at all.

> **A zero-set functional is either analytic — hence evaluable by the explicit formula, hence a
> combination of prime and archimedean data subject to the three-way cancellation — or non-analytic,
> hence able to detect the critical line but not computable from arithmetic.  The two are mutually
> exclusive, and every criterion in this development falls on one side or the other.**

This is why every criterion examined is either arithmetic and blind, or exact and inert.  It is a
statement about the shape of the problem rather than about any method.

This file formalizes the identity-theorem obstruction and the vanishing of the reflection weight on
the critical line.
-/

open Complex Filter Topology

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

/-- **The identity-theorem obstruction.**  An entire function vanishing on the whole critical line
vanishes identically: the line is not discrete, so it accumulates. -/
theorem entire_vanishing_on_criticalLine_eq_zero {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f Set.univ)
    (hline : ∀ s : ℂ, s.re = 1 / 2 → f s = 0) :
    Set.EqOn f 0 Set.univ := by
  set z₀ : ℂ := ⟨1 / 2, 0⟩ with hz₀
  have hz₀re : z₀.re = 1 / 2 := rfl
  set r : ℕ → ℝ := fun n => 1 / (n + 1 : ℝ) with hr
  have hrpos : ∀ n, 0 < r n := fun n => by simp only [hr]; positivity
  set u : ℕ → ℂ := fun n => ⟨1 / 2, r n⟩ with hu
  have hure : ∀ n, (u n).re = 1 / 2 := fun n => rfl
  have hune : ∀ n, u n ≠ z₀ := by
    intro n h
    have him : (u n).im = z₀.im := by rw [h]
    have hpos := hrpos n
    simp only [hu, hz₀] at him
    linarith [him ▸ hpos]
  have htend : Tendsto u atTop (𝓝[≠] z₀) := by
    rw [tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff]
    constructor
    · rw [tendsto_iff_dist_tendsto_zero]
      have hdist : ∀ n : ℕ, dist (u n) z₀ = r n := by
        intro n
        rw [Complex.dist_eq]
        have hrep : u n - z₀ = ((r n : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I := by
          apply Complex.ext <;> simp [hu, hz₀]
        rw [hrep, norm_mul, Complex.norm_I, mul_one, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs,
          abs_of_pos (hrpos n)]
      simp only [hdist, hr]
      exact tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat
    · exact Eventually.of_forall (fun n => hune n)
  have hfreq : ∃ᶠ z : ℂ in 𝓝[≠] z₀, f z = 0 :=
    htend.frequently (Frequently.of_forall (fun n => hline (u n) (hure n)))
  exact hf.eqOn_zero_of_preconnected_of_frequently_eq_zero
    isPreconnected_univ (Set.mem_univ z₀) hfreq

/-- **The reflection weight vanishes on the critical line.**  For `Re ρ = 1/2` the reflected point
`1 - ρ̄` equals `ρ`, so any difference of weights at the two points is zero. -/
theorem reflection_fixes_criticalLine {s : ℂ} (hs : s.re = 1 / 2) :
    1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) s = s := by
  apply Complex.ext
  · simp [Complex.sub_re, hs]
    linarith [hs]
  · simp [Complex.sub_im]

/-- Hence the reflection difference vanishes exactly on the line, which by the identity theorem makes
it non-analytic unless identically zero. -/
theorem reflection_difference_zero_on_line {φ : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (hs : s.re = 1 / 2) :
    φ s - φ (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) s) = 0 := by
  rw [reflection_fixes_criticalLine hs]
  ring

/-- **Off the line the reflection moves the point.**  If `Re s ≠ 1/2` then `1 - s̄ ≠ s`, so a weight
injective in the real part gives a nonzero difference. -/
theorem reflection_moves_offLine {s : ℂ} (hs : s.re ≠ 1 / 2) :
    1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) s ≠ s := by
  intro h
  apply hs
  have hre : (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) s).re = s.re := by rw [h]
  simp [Complex.sub_re] at hre
  linarith

end RHTower

/-- **The second-derivative log-derivative identity for Γ.**  At any point where `Γ` is twice
differentiable and nonzero, `Γ''·Γ − (Γ')² = Γ²·(Γ'/Γ)'` — the numerator of the quotient rule for the
log-derivative `ψ = Γ'/Γ`.  This is the algebraic core connecting Γ's second-order jet to the digamma:
the combination `Γ·Γ'' − (Γ')²`, which is exactly the leading obstruction in the mixed
`(Γ')²`/`Γ·Γ''` tie, equals `Γ²·ψ'`. -/
theorem gamma_secondDeriv_logDeriv_identity (s : ℂ) (hs : Complex.Gamma s ≠ 0)
    (h1 : DifferentiableAt ℂ Complex.Gamma s) (h2 : DifferentiableAt ℂ (deriv Complex.Gamma) s) :
    iteratedDeriv 2 Complex.Gamma s * Complex.Gamma s - (deriv Complex.Gamma s)^2
      = (Complex.Gamma s)^2 * deriv (fun z => deriv Complex.Gamma z / Complex.Gamma z) s := by
  have hdd : deriv (fun z => deriv Complex.Gamma z / Complex.Gamma z) s
      = (deriv (deriv Complex.Gamma) s * Complex.Gamma s
        - deriv Complex.Gamma s * deriv Complex.Gamma s) / (Complex.Gamma s)^2 :=
    deriv_div h2 h1 hs
  rw [hdd, show iteratedDeriv 2 Complex.Gamma s = deriv (deriv Complex.Gamma) s from by
    rw [iteratedDeriv_succ, iteratedDeriv_one]]
  field_simp

/-- **The mixed three-variable relation reduces to a first-order relation in the digamma jet.**  If
`α(s)·(Γ')² + β(s)·(Γ''·Γ) = 0` at a point where `Γ` is twice differentiable and nonzero, then
`(α+β)(s)·ψ² + β(s)·ψ' = 0` there, for the log-derivative `ψ = Γ'/Γ` (digamma).  Substituting the
identity `Γ·Γ'' = (Γ')² + Γ²·ψ'` and dividing by `Γ²` collapses the three jet variables `(Γ,Γ',Γ'')`
— where the `(Γ')²`/`Γ·Γ''` monomial tie obstructs the residue method — to two jet variables `(ψ,ψ')`.
This is the bridge that turns the sole remaining tie-obstructed case of Hölder's theorem for `Γ` into a
differential-non-existence question for the digamma. -/
theorem gamma_mixed_reduces_to_digamma (α β : Polynomial ℂ) (s : ℂ) (hs : Complex.Gamma s ≠ 0)
    (h1 : DifferentiableAt ℂ Complex.Gamma s) (h2 : DifferentiableAt ℂ (deriv Complex.Gamma) s)
    (hrel : α.eval s * (deriv Complex.Gamma s)^2
      + β.eval s * (iteratedDeriv 2 Complex.Gamma s * Complex.Gamma s) = 0) :
    (α.eval s + β.eval s) * (deriv Complex.Gamma s / Complex.Gamma s)^2
      + β.eval s * deriv (fun z => deriv Complex.Gamma z / Complex.Gamma z) s = 0 := by
  have hid := gamma_secondDeriv_logDeriv_identity s hs h1 h2
  have hΓ2 : (Complex.Gamma s)^2 ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero 2 hs
  field_simp
  have key : α.eval s * (deriv Complex.Gamma s)^2
      + β.eval s * (iteratedDeriv 2 Complex.Gamma s * Complex.Gamma s) = 0 := hrel
  rw [show iteratedDeriv 2 Complex.Gamma s * Complex.Gamma s
    = (deriv Complex.Gamma s)^2 + (Complex.Gamma s)^2 * deriv (fun z => deriv Complex.Gamma z / Complex.Gamma z) s
    from by linear_combination hid] at key
  linear_combination key

/-- **The leading constraint on the mixed three-variable relation.**  If
`α(s)·(Γ')² + β(s)·(Γ''·Γ) = 0` off the poles, then `α + 2β = 0` as polynomials.  The two monomials
`(Γ')²` and `Γ·Γ''` both have weighted degree `4` and total degree `2` — the genuine tie — so at each
pole `−k` their leading Laurent coefficients add on the *same* power `r_k²`: multiplying by `(s+k)⁴` and
letting `s → −k` gives `(α(−k) + 2β(−k))·r_k² = 0`, hence `α(−k) + 2β(−k) = 0` for every `k` (residues
`(s+k)²Γ' → −r_k`, `(s+k)Γ·(s+k)³Γ'' → 2r_k²`).  Since `α + 2β` vanishes at the infinitely many points
`−k`, it is the zero polynomial.  Combined with the identity `Γ·Γ'' − 2(Γ')² = Γ²·(ψ' − ψ²)`
(`gamma_secondDeriv_logDeriv_identity`), this reduces the mixed case to `β·Γ²·(ψ' − ψ²) = 0`: the whole
tie collapses to `β = 0` once `ψ' − ψ²` (digamma) is shown not identically zero — the sole surviving
crux of Hölder's theorem for `Γ` in three jet variables. -/
theorem gamma_mixed_leading (α β : Polynomial ℂ)
    (hrel : ∀ s : ℂ, (∀ m : ℕ, s ≠ -(m:ℂ)) →
      α.eval s * (deriv Complex.Gamma s)^2
        + β.eval s * (iteratedDeriv 2 Complex.Gamma s * Complex.Gamma s) = 0) :
    α + 2 * β = 0 := by
  have hroot : ∀ k : ℕ, (α + 2 * β).eval (-(k:ℂ)) = 0 := by
    intro k
    have hlim0 : Tendsto (fun s : ℂ => (s + (k:ℂ))^4 *
        (α.eval s * (deriv Complex.Gamma s)^2
          + β.eval s * (iteratedDeriv 2 Complex.Gamma s * Complex.Gamma s)))
        (𝓝[≠] (-(k:ℂ))) (𝓝 0) := by
      have hev : ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝[≠] (-(k:ℂ)), (s + (k:ℂ))^4 *
          (α.eval s * (deriv Complex.Gamma s)^2
            + β.eval s * (iteratedDeriv 2 Complex.Gamma s * Complex.Gamma s)) = 0 := by
        filter_upwards [eventually_nhdsWithin_of_eventually_nhds
          (Metric.ball_mem_nhds (-(k:ℂ)) (show (0:ℝ) < 1/2 by norm_num)), self_mem_nhdsWithin]
          with s hsb hsne
        simp only [Set.mem_compl_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hsne
        rw [hrel s (ball_avoids hsb hsne), mul_zero]
      exact tendsto_const_nhds.congr' (hev.mono (fun _ h => h.symm))
    have hcα : Tendsto (fun s : ℂ => α.eval s) (𝓝[≠] (-(k:ℂ))) (𝓝 (α.eval (-(k:ℂ)))) :=
      α.continuous.continuousAt.continuousWithinAt

import Mathlib

/-!
# Montgomery--Vaughan weighted Hilbert inequality interface

`MVHilbert C` states the bilinear weighted Hilbert inequality for an arbitrary
finite family of distinct real frequencies and any positive admissible gap
weights.  The implementation in this directory proves the statement with an
explicit constant.
-/

noncomputable section

open Complex
open scoped BigOperators ComplexConjugate

namespace RiemannGaussian

/-- The bilinear weighted Montgomery--Vaughan inequality with constant `C`.
The weights may be any positive lower bounds for the pairwise frequency gaps. -/
def MVHilbert (C : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (freq δ : ι → ℝ) (x z : ι → ℂ),
    Function.Injective freq → (∀ r, 0 < δ r) →
      (∀ r s, r ≠ s → δ r ≤ |freq r - freq s|) →
    ‖∑ r, ∑ s, if r = s then (0 : ℂ)
        else x r * conj (z s) / ((freq r - freq s : ℝ) : ℂ)‖
      ≤ C * Real.sqrt (∑ r, ‖x r‖ ^ 2 / δ r) *
          Real.sqrt (∑ r, ‖z r‖ ^ 2 / δ r)

end RiemannGaussian

end

/-!
# Local-to-global RH tomography

Publication capstone joining two unconditional theorem surfaces:

* the cofinite reflected-Lambert local-factor orbit and its continuous
  compact-open classifier obstruction;
* fixed-width logarithmic Weil tomography and its exact finite
  prime--Gamma source realization.

The first surface proves that a continuous finite-factor-invariant local
germ cannot classify the source Hankel sign.  The second supplies a global
weighted-tail observable which is RH-complete and recovers the full
off-critical divisor with analytic multiplicity.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

/-- The local source-Hankel sign and every positive-width rectangular
logarithmic Weil sequence are exact RH classifiers.  Their information
behavior differs: the former cannot descend through the continuous
finite-factor local quotient, whereas the latter retains the global
weighted tail. -/
theorem localGlobal_two_exact_RH_classifiers
    {L : ℝ} (hL : 0 < L) :
    (PrimeArchSourceTraceHankelIntNonnegative ↔ RiemannHypothesis) ∧
    (RiemannHypothesis ↔
      ∀ n : ℕ, 0 ≤
        (xiWeilPolarization
          (xiRectangularTwoEdgeTransform L (Real.log n / 2))
          (xiRectangularTwoEdgeTransform L (Real.log n / 2))).re) := by
  exact ⟨primeArchSourceTraceHankelIntNonnegative_iff_riemannHypothesis,
    riemannHypothesis_iff_rectangular_logSample_weil_nonneg hL⟩

end RHTower

/-!
# Finite fibres of decorated Stokes characteristic data

This module proves the finite-type core of the decorated finite-fibre theorem.  For fixed
ramification and first exponent, the full strict characteristic type is finite.  Strict divisor
chains are finite at fixed ramification.  Finally, fixing weighted irregularity leaves only
finitely many complete characteristic data.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions
namespace IrregularStokes

namespace Characteristic

/-- The first exponent is bounded by the full weighted irregularity. -/
theorem firstExponent_le_weightedIrregularity {R beta : ℕ} (c : Characteristic R beta) :
    beta ≤ c.weightedIrregularity := by
  have hdrop : 1 ≤ R - c.nextRamification := by
    have := c.nextRamification_lt
    omega
  have hmul : beta ≤ beta * (R - c.nextRamification) := by
    calc
      beta = beta * 1 := by simp
      _ ≤ beta * (R - c.nextRamification) := Nat.mul_le_mul_left beta hdrop
  exact hmul.trans c.firstContribution_le_weightedIrregularity

/-- Finite constructor code for a characteristic with fixed initial indices. -/
private def Code (R beta : ℕ) : Type :=
  { _u : Unit // 1 < R ∧ 0 < beta ∧ Nat.gcd R beta = 1 } ⊕
  (Σ E : Fin R, Σ gamma : Fin beta,
    { _tail : Characteristic E gamma //
      (1 : ℕ) < (E : ℕ) ∧ 0 < beta ∧ Nat.gcd R beta = (E : ℕ) })

/-- Full characteristic data form a finite type once ramification and first exponent are fixed. -/
theorem finite (R beta : ℕ) : Finite (Characteristic R beta) := by
  revert beta
  induction R using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | h R ih =>
      intro beta
      letI tailFinite (E : Fin R) (gamma : Fin beta) :
          Finite (Characteristic (E : ℕ) (gamma : ℕ)) :=
        ih (E : ℕ) E.isLt (gamma : ℕ)
      let decode : Code R beta → Characteristic R beta
        | .inl h => Characteristic.terminal h.property.1 h.property.2.1 h.property.2.2
        | .inr ⟨E, gamma, tail⟩ =>
            Characteristic.step E.isLt tail.property.1 tail.property.2.1 tail.property.2.2
              gamma.isLt tail.1
      haveI : Finite (Code R beta) := by
        unfold Code
        infer_instance
      apply Finite.of_surjective decode
      intro c
      cases c with
      | terminal hR hbeta hgcd =>
          exact ⟨Sum.inl ⟨(), hR, hbeta, hgcd⟩, rfl⟩
      | @step R E beta gamma hER hE hbeta hgcd hgamma tail =>
          exact ⟨Sum.inr ⟨⟨E, hER⟩, ⟨gamma, hgamma⟩, ⟨tail, hE, hbeta, hgcd⟩⟩, rfl⟩

end Characteristic

/-- Strict divisor chains at fixed ramification form a finite type. -/
theorem finite_strictDivisorChain (R : ℕ) : Finite (StrictDivisorChain R) := by
  let Encoding := Σ beta : Fin (2 * R), Characteristic R beta
  let encode : StrictDivisorChain R → Encoding := fun d =>
    ⟨⟨d.firstExponent, d.firstExponent_lt_twice⟩, d.toCharacteristic⟩
  let decode : Encoding → StrictDivisorChain R := fun e => e.2.toStrictDivisorChain
  have hleft : Function.LeftInverse decode encode := by
    intro d
    exact d.toStrictDivisorChain_toCharacteristic
  letI characteristicFinite (beta : Fin (2 * R)) : Finite (Characteristic R beta) :=
    Characteristic.finite R beta
  haveI : Finite Encoding := inferInstance
  exact Finite.of_injective encode hleft.injective

/-- Complete local characteristic data with fixed ramification and weighted irregularity. -/
structure FixedWeightedCharacteristic (R W : ℕ) where
  firstExponent : ℕ
  characteristic : Characteristic R firstExponent
  weighted_eq : characteristic.weightedIrregularity = W

/-- Fixed diagonal multiplicity and fixed ramification leave only finitely many local
characteristic data. -/
theorem finite_fixedWeightedCharacteristic (R W : ℕ) :
    Finite (FixedWeightedCharacteristic R W) := by
  let Encoding := Σ beta : Fin (W + 1),
    { c : Characteristic R beta // c.weightedIrregularity = W }
  let encode : FixedWeightedCharacteristic R W → Encoding := fun c =>
    ⟨⟨c.firstExponent, Nat.lt_succ_of_le <| by
        calc
          c.firstExponent ≤ c.characteristic.weightedIrregularity :=
            c.characteristic.firstExponent_le_weightedIrregularity
          _ = W := c.weighted_eq⟩,
      ⟨c.characteristic, c.weighted_eq⟩⟩
  let decode : Encoding → FixedWeightedCharacteristic R W := fun e =>
    { firstExponent := e.1
      characteristic := e.2.1
      weighted_eq := e.2.2 }
  have hleft : Function.LeftInverse decode encode := by
    rintro ⟨beta, c, hw⟩
    rfl
  letI characteristicFinite (beta : Fin (W + 1)) : Finite (Characteristic R beta) :=
    Characteristic.finite R beta
  haveI : Finite Encoding := inferInstance
  exact Finite.of_injective encode hleft.injective

end IrregularStokes
end GaloisForLFunctions

/-!
# Positive variation energy of the completed error forces RH

The positive excess in the dyadic weighted-prime inequality is exactly the positive part of one
backward `log 2` difference of the completed critical-Mellin error, including its explicit
decaying endpoint value.  Consequently pointwise subpower control is unnecessary: weighted
Dirichlet energy, or weighted square energy, of only these positive variations already implies RH.
-/

open Complex Filter Function Set LSeries

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

/-- The positive excess in the dyadic weighted-prime inequality is exactly the positive backward
variation of the completed critical-Mellin error. -/
theorem dyadicWeightedPrimeWindowPositiveExcess_eq_posPart_completedErrorBackwardDifference
    {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    dyadicWeightedPrimeWindowPositiveExcess n =
      (criticalMellinCompletedError (Real.log n - Real.log 2) -
          criticalMellinCompletedError (Real.log n) +
          2 * (Real.sqrt 2 - 1) / Real.sqrt n)⁺ := by
  rw [dyadicWeightedPrimeWindowPositiveExcess,
    dyadicWeightedPrimeWindow_eq_floorSum,
    dyadicWeightedPrimeWindow_eq_main_add_completedErrorDifference hn]
  congr 1
  ring

/-- Positive backward completed-error variation, with the irrelevant finite prefix normalized to
the already-defined positive excess so the identity is exact at every natural index. -/
def dyadicCompletedErrorBackwardPositiveVariation (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  if 2 ≤ n then
    (criticalMellinCompletedError (Real.log n - Real.log 2) -
        criticalMellinCompletedError (Real.log n) +
        2 * (Real.sqrt 2 - 1) / Real.sqrt n)⁺
  else
    dyadicWeightedPrimeWindowPositiveExcess n

theorem dyadicCompletedErrorBackwardPositiveVariation_eq_positiveExcess
    (n : ℕ) :
    dyadicCompletedErrorBackwardPositiveVariation n =
      dyadicWeightedPrimeWindowPositiveExcess n := by
  by_cases hn : 2 ≤ n
  · rw [dyadicCompletedErrorBackwardPositiveVariation, if_pos hn,
      dyadicWeightedPrimeWindowPositiveExcess_eq_posPart_completedErrorBackwardDifference hn]
  · rw [dyadicCompletedErrorBackwardPositiveVariation, if_neg hn]

/-- **Positive-variation energy gate.**  Weighted Dirichlet energy of only the positive backward
variations of the completed error, at every abscissa right of one, implies RH. -/
theorem riemannHypothesis_of_completedErrorBackwardPositiveVariationEnergy
    (henergy : ∀ epsilon : ℝ, 0 < epsilon →
      LSeriesSummable
        (fun n => ((dyadicCompletedErrorBackwardPositiveVariation n : ℝ) : ℂ))
        (((1 + epsilon : ℝ) : ℂ))) :
    RiemannHypothesis := by
  apply riemannHypothesis_of_dyadicWeightedPrimeWindowPositiveExcessEnergy
  intro epsilon hepsilon
  simpa only [dyadicCompletedErrorBackwardPositiveVariation_eq_positiveExcess] using
    henergy epsilon hepsilon

/-- Weighted square energy of the same positive completed-error variations is already sufficient
for RH.  This is the Hilbert-space form of the value criterion. -/
theorem riemannHypothesis_of_completedErrorBackwardPositiveVariationSquareEnergy
    (h2 : ∀ epsilon : ℝ, 0 < epsilon →
      Summable
        (realDirichletWeightedTerm
          (fun n => (dyadicCompletedErrorBackwardPositiveVariation n) ^ 2)
          (1 + epsilon))) :
    RiemannHypothesis := by
  apply riemannHypothesis_of_dyadicWeightedPrimeWindowPositiveExcessSquareEnergy
  intro epsilon hepsilon
  simpa only [dyadicCompletedErrorBackwardPositiveVariation_eq_positiveExcess] using
    h2 epsilon hepsilon

/-- **Critical positive-variation endpoint.**  Pointwise control is unnecessary: absolute
Dirichlet summability at the single critical abscissa `1` of only the positive backward
variations of the completed error already proves RH. -/
theorem riemannHypothesis_of_completedErrorBackwardPositiveVariation_summable_at_one
    (henergy : LSeriesSummable
      (fun n => ((dyadicCompletedErrorBackwardPositiveVariation n : ℝ) : ℂ)) 1) :
    RiemannHypothesis := by
  apply riemannHypothesis_of_dyadicWeightedPrimeWindowPositiveExcess_summable_at_one
  simpa only [dyadicCompletedErrorBackwardPositiveVariation_eq_positiveExcess] using henergy

end RHTower
