/-!
# Weighted orbit induction: norm, reduced gap, and closed range

A bounded scalar amplitude family `a` weights the transported blocks of an orbit induction.  This
module proves the exact operator-norm law `(WOI.3)`, the kernel identification, the transverse
lower bound `(WOI.4)`, and the closed-range classification `(WOI.5)`: the weighted induction has
closed range exactly when the local operator does **and** the amplitudes have a uniform nonzero
gap.  It then develops the finite truncations of the amplitude family, the tail supremum
`tailSup a = ⨅_F ⨆_{i ∉ F} |a i|`, and proves `(WOI.7)`: the essential norm of the weighted
induction is exactly `tailSup a · ‖D‖` whenever the local block is compact.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open Filter RHTower
open scoped ENNReal Topology InnerProductSpace

noncomputable section

section Weighted

variable {I : Type} [Nonempty I] {H K : Type*}
  [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H]
  [NormedAddCommGroup K] [InnerProductSpace ℂ K] [CompleteSpace K]

/-- `(WOI.1)`  The transported block scaled by the source amplitude. -/
def weightedBlock (a : I → ℂ) (D : H →L[ℂ] K) (U : I → (H ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H))
    (V : I → (K ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] K)) (i : I) : H →L[ℂ] K := a i • orbitBlock D U V i

omit [Nonempty I] [CompleteSpace H] [CompleteSpace K] in
@[simp] theorem weightedBlock_apply (a : I → ℂ) (D : H →L[ℂ] K) (U : I → (H ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H))
    (V : I → (K ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] K)) (i : I) (x : H) :
    weightedBlock a D U V i x = a i • V i (D ((U i).symm x)) := rfl

omit [Nonempty I] [CompleteSpace H] [CompleteSpace K] in
theorem norm_weightedBlock (a : I → ℂ) (D : H →L[ℂ] K) (U : I → (H ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H))
    (V : I → (K ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] K)) (i : I) :
    ‖weightedBlock a D U V i‖ = ‖a i‖ * ‖D‖ := by
  rw [weightedBlock, norm_smul, norm_orbitBlock]

/-- `(WOI.2)`  The amplitude supremum `‖a‖_∞`. -/
def ampSup (a : I → ℂ) : ℝ := ⨆ i, ‖a i‖

omit [Nonempty I] in
theorem le_ampSup {a : I → ℂ} (hbdd : BddAbove (Set.range fun i => ‖a i‖)) (i : I) :
    ‖a i‖ ≤ ampSup a := le_ciSup hbdd i

theorem ampSup_nonneg {a : I → ℂ} (hbdd : BddAbove (Set.range fun i => ‖a i‖)) :
    0 ≤ ampSup a :=
  le_trans (norm_nonneg _) (le_ampSup hbdd (Classical.arbitrary I))

theorem ampSup_le {a : I → ℂ} {c : ℝ} (h : ∀ i, ‖a i‖ ≤ c) : ampSup a ≤ c :=
  ciSup_le h

/-- `(WOI.1)`  The weighted orbit induction. -/
def weightedInduction (a : I → ℂ) (D : H →L[ℂ] K) (U : I → (H ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H))
    (V : I → (K ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] K)) (hbdd : BddAbove (Set.range fun i => ‖a i‖)) :
    lp (fun _ : I => H) 2 →L[ℂ] lp (fun _ : I => K) 2 :=
  rectangularBlockOperator (E := fun _ : I => H) (F := fun _ : I => K)
    (fun i => weightedBlock a D U V i)
    (mul_nonneg (ampSup_nonneg hbdd) (norm_nonneg D))
    (fun i => by
      rw [norm_weightedBlock]
      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (le_ampSup hbdd i) (norm_nonneg D))

omit [CompleteSpace H] [CompleteSpace K] in
@[simp] theorem weightedInduction_apply (a : I → ℂ) (D : H →L[ℂ] K) (U : I → (H ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H))
    (V : I → (K ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] K)) (hbdd : BddAbove (Set.range fun i => ‖a i‖))
    (x : lp (fun _ : I => H) 2) (i : I) :
    weightedInduction a D U V hbdd x i = a i • V i (D ((U i).symm (x i))) := rfl

omit [CompleteSpace H] [CompleteSpace K] in
theorem weightedInduction_single [DecidableEq I] (a : I → ℂ) (D : H →L[ℂ] K)
    (U : I → (H ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H)) (V : I → (K ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] K))
    (hbdd : BddAbove (Set.range fun i => ‖a i‖)) (i : I) (x : H) :
    weightedInduction a D U V hbdd (lp.single 2 i x)
      = lp.single 2 i (weightedBlock a D U V i x) :=
  rectangularBlockOperator_single (E := fun _ : I => H) (F := fun _ : I => K) _ _ _ i x

omit [CompleteSpace H] [CompleteSpace K] in
theorem norm_weightedInduction_le (a : I → ℂ) (D : H →L[ℂ] K) (U : I → (H ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H))
    (V : I → (K ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] K)) (hbdd : BddAbove (Set.range fun i => ‖a i‖)) :
    ‖weightedInduction a D U V hbdd‖ ≤ ampSup a * ‖D‖ := by
  refine LinearMap.mkContinuous_norm_le _
    (mul_nonneg (ampSup_nonneg hbdd) (norm_nonneg D)) ?_
  exact rectangularBlockOperatorLinear_norm_le _ _ _

omit [CompleteSpace H] [CompleteSpace K] in
theorem norm_weightedBlock_le_norm_weightedInduction [DecidableEq I] (a : I → ℂ)
    (D : H →L[ℂ] K) (U : I → (H ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] H)) (V : I → (K ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] K))
    (hbdd : BddAbove (Set.range fun i => ‖a i‖)) (i : I) :
    ‖a i‖ * ‖D‖ ≤ ‖weightedInduction a D U V hbdd‖ := by
  rw [← norm_weightedBlock a D U V i]
  refine ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound _
    (norm_nonneg (weightedInduction a D U V hbdd)) fun x => ?_
  have h := (weightedInduction a D U V hbdd).le_opNorm (lp.single 2 i x)
  rw [weightedInduction_single a D U V hbdd i x] at h
  have h1 : ‖(lp.single 2 i (weightedBlock a D U V i x) : lp (fun _ : I => K) 2)‖
      = ‖weightedBlock a D U V i x‖ :=
    lp.norm_single (E := fun _ : I => K) (by norm_num) i _
  have h2 : ‖(lp.single 2 i x : lp (fun _ : I => H) 2)‖ = ‖x‖ :=
    lp.norm_single (E := fun _ : I => H) (by norm_num) i x
  rw [h1, h2] at h
  exact h

prose.text:
sequences and the exact obstruction
* **Recovers the known case.** `m = 1`, `δ_1 = 1`: `u = 1/⌈τ⌉`, giving `LV ≤ ⌈τ⌉(2−2σ)` — Guth's
  "Conjecture 3.4 is known when `T` is an integer power of `N`". ✔
* **Extends it to all rational `τ`, for free convolutions.** For `τ = b/a` (`a ≤ b` integers), take
  `m = a` factors with `δ_i = 1/a` and `p_i = b`: then `τ/δ_i = b ∈ ℤ` and `u = a/b = 1/τ`, giving
  `LV ≤ (2−2σ)τ` exactly. By monotonicity and density of the rationals this yields
  ```
        \mathrm{LV}^{\mathrm{div}}(σ,τ) ≤ (2−2σ)τ  \text{ for ALL real } τ ≥ 1
  ```
  when the coefficient class is *balanced `a`-fold convolutions*. **That is Montgomery's `ℓ^q`
  conjecture — hence the Density Hypothesis — for that class.**
* **Why this does not prove DH.** In the zero-detection reduction the length exponents `δ_i` are
  **produced by the problem**, not chosen: dyadic pigeonholing fixes them, and Heath-Brown/Vaughan
  identities give a whole range of configurations, all of which must be handled. For a generic
  configuration `τ/δ_i ∉ ℤ` and the method loses exactly `(1/τ)/u = ∏`-type rounding.
> **THE OBSTRUCTION, STATED EXACTLY:** *the Density Hypothesis via the Hölder–moment method is
> equivalent to a Diophantine matching condition — every length configuration `(δ_i)` arising from the
> decomposition must satisfy `τ/δ_i ∈ ℤ`. The failure is pure rounding: `⌈τ/δ_i⌉` versus `τ/δ_i`.*
`[OPEN CORE 32]` Two ways out, both new: **(a)** engineer the decomposition (choice of Heath-Brown
order and range subdivision) so that the surviving configurations have `τ/δ_i` integral — a
combinatorial design problem, not an analytic one; **(b)** replace the integer power `p_i` by a
fractional one, i.e. find a substitute for "`A^{p}` is a Dirichlet polynomial with divisor-bounded
coefficients" valid for non-integer `p`. *(Recorded: interpolating the moments log-convexly between
`⌊p⌋` and `⌈p⌉` gives exponent `f(p)=3τ−3+p(2−τ−σ)` in the two-factor case, which never beats the
mean value theorem — checked at `(σ,τ)=(7/10,6/5)`: `0.8` versus the required `0.72`.)*

## Theorem 23 (optimality of the Hölder–moment method) `[PROVED HERE]`
Allowing `p_i < τ/δ_i` as well (so that Montgomery–Vaughan gives `(T·N^{p_iδ_i})^{1/p_i}` instead of
`N^{2δ_i}`), the method yields
```
     \mathrm{LV}(σ,τ) ≤ \frac{1 + ∑_i \max(δ_i,\ τ/p_i) - 2σ}{∑_i 1/p_i} .
```
Writing `S = \{i : p_i < τ/δ_i\}`, `A = ∑_{S}δ_i`, `G = ∑_S 1/p_i`, `z := τG − A ≥ 0`, this simplifies
to
```
        \mathrm{LV}(σ,τ) ≤ τ\,\frac{(2−2σ)+z}{1+z} ,
```
which for `σ > 1/2` is **strictly increasing in `z`**. Hence `z = 0` is optimal, the method can never
do better than `(2−2σ)τ`, and it attains that value **exactly** when every `τ/δ_i` is an integer.
> **So `(2−2σ)τ` — the Density-Hypothesis requirement — is precisely the ceiling of the entire
> Hölder–moment family, and the only thing standing between the method and DH is integrality of
> `τ/δ_i`.** Nothing analytic is missing; the deficit is arithmetic rounding.

## `[OPEN CORE 32(a)]` — the design that would supply integral lengths `[NEW]`
The standard detection uses `M(s)=∑_{m≤y}μ(m)m^{-s}`, giving coefficients `c = μ_{≤y}∗1`: a **2-fold**
convolution whose split `(N_1,N_2)` is fixed by dyadic pigeonholing, hence uncontrollable.
**Replace it by a `k`-fold factored mollifier**
```
        M(s) = ∏_{i=1}^{k} M_i(s) ,  M_i(s) = ∑_{m ≤ y^{1/k}} μ_i(m)\,m^{-s},
        \text{with } M_i \text{ approximating } ζ(s)^{-1/k} ,
```
so that `ζM − 1` has coefficients which are a `(k+1)`-fold convolution with **`k` factors of
prescribed length `y^{1/k}`** — lengths chosen by us, not by the pigeonhole. Then `δ_i = (1/k)\log_N y`
for `i=1..k` and `δ_0 = 1 − \log_N y`, and one may solve
```
        τ/δ_i = kτ/\log_N y ∈ ℤ ,\qquad τ/δ_0 = τ/(1-\log_N y) ∈ ℤ
```
by choosing `\log_N y` and `k`. For `τ = 3/2` the choice `\log_N y = 1/2`, `k = 1` already gives
`δ_0 = δ_1 = 1/2`, `τ/δ_i = 3 ∈ ℤ`, `u = 2/3 = 1/τ` — **exactly the balanced configuration that
Theorem 22 shows yields `LV ≤ (2−2σ)τ`, i.e. the Density Hypothesis at `τ = 3/2`.**
`[OPEN CORE 33]` The remaining work is analytic bookkeeping of a kind that is standard in the
mollifier literature but has never been combined with the Hölder–moment method: (i) construct
`M_i ≈ ζ^{-1/k}` with divisor-bounded coefficients (the coefficients of `ζ^{-1/k}` are
`≪_ε n^{ε}`, so this is available); (ii) control the error `ζM − 1` when `M` is a *truncated product*
rather than a truncated Dirichlet series — the truncation error of `∏M_i` is the new term, and it is
the only place where the design can fail; (iii) verify that the `ζ`-side factor `δ_0` can be given an
integral `τ/δ_0` simultaneously, or else handled by `\mathrm{LV}_ζ` (which is *vacuous* in
Corollary 11.9 at `τ_0 = 3/2`).
**This is the first concrete design in this card that would, if it closes, give the Density
Hypothesis outright rather than a reduction.**

R` one-separated `t_r ∈ [T,2T]`:
```
   (P_k)\ \ R ≪ T^{(2−2σ)kη+o(1)}\quad (k ≥ 1/η,\ \text{length } N^{k} ≥ T) ,
   (M_k)\ \ R ≪ T^{1+kη(1−2σ)+o(1)}\quad (k ≤ 1/η,\ \text{length } N^{k} ≤ T) .
```
**The `η > 1/2` window is completely resolved by reflection.** For `N ≥ T^{1/2}` the B-process gives
`|D_N| = |G_M| + O(T^{o(1)})` with `M = T/N ≤ T^{1/2}`, and computing the fourth moment on the *dual*
side (where `M² ≤ T`, so the mean value theorem is diagonal) gives
```
      ∑_{r}|D_N(t_r)|^{4} = ∑_r |G_M(t_r)|^4 ≪ T\cdot\frac{T^2}{M^2}\,T^{o(1)} = T\,N^{2}\,T^{o(1)} ,
```
strictly better than the direct `N^4` whenever `N² > T`. Hence `(M_2)` holds for **all** `η`, and
```
        R ≪ T^{1+2η(1−2σ)+o(1)} ≤ T^{2−2σ+o(1)} \iff η ≥ 1/2 .
```
So every scale `η ∈ [1/2,1)` satisfies the Density-Hypothesis bound outright. `[PROVED HERE]`

## The deficit, exactly `[PROVED HERE]`
On the window `η ∈ (1/(k+1), 1/k)` (`k ≥ 2`, i.e. `τ = 1/η ∈ (k,k+1)`), the best available bound is
`\min\big((2−2σ)(k+1)η,\ 1+kη(1−2σ)\big)`, whose maximum over the window is at the crossing
```
        η_k = \frac{1}{k+2−2σ} ,\qquad \text{value}\quad E_k(σ) = \frac{(2−2σ)(k+1)}{k+2−2σ} ,
```
so `E_k(σ) > 2−2σ` for every `k`, with `E_k ↓ 2−2σ` as `k → ∞`:
```
   σ = 7/10:\quad E_2 = 9/13 = 0.6923\ (τ = 13/5),\quad E_3 = 2/3,\quad E_4 = 0.6522,\quad
                  E_{10} = 0.6226,\quad E_∞ = 3/5 .
```
`\mathrm{A}(σ)(1−σ) ≤ \max_k E_k(σ) = E_2(σ) = \frac{3(1−σ)}{2−σ}`, i.e. `\mathrm{A}(σ) ≤ 3/(2−σ)` —
**Ingham's theorem, recovered exactly, with the location of its bottleneck identified as
`τ = 4 − 2σ`** (`= 13/5` at `σ = 7/10`).
> ### The picture, complete
> * `η ∈ [1/2, 1)` (`τ ∈ (1,2]`): **resolved** — reflection + fourth moment give exactly `2−2σ`, with
>   strict improvement for `η > 1/2`.
> * `η ∈ (1/(k+1), 1/k)`, `k ≥ 2`: **deficit `E_k(σ) − (2−2σ) = \frac{(2−2σ)(1−(2−2σ))}{k+2−2σ}`**,
>   which is `> 0` for `σ > 1/2` and decays like `1/k`.
> * `η = 1/k` exactly: **resolved** — `(P_k)` gives `(2−2σ)` on the nose.
> So the unresolved set is a union of open intervals `(1/(k+1), 1/k)` accumulating at `0`, and the
> Density Hypothesis is precisely the assertion that the moment bound can be interpolated *across each
> gap between consecutive integer powers*. The deficit is largest on the **first** gap `τ ∈ (2,3)`.
`[OPEN CORE 53]` Everything now rests on one bounded, explicit question:
> **For `τ ∈ (2,3)` and `1/2 < σ < 1`, is `\mathrm{LV}_ζ(σ,τ) ≤ (2−2σ)τ`?**
Beating `E_2(σ)` on this single window improves `‖A‖_∞` below `30/13`; proving it for all `k` is the
Density Hypothesis. The `k`-th window needs the `k`-th and `(k+1)`-st moments to be *interpolated*, and
the reflection already achieves exactly this interpolation for `k = 1`. **The natural conjecture is
that the reflection has a `k`-fold analogue** — a transform under which a block of scale
`η ∈ (1/(k+1),1/k)` is exchanged for one at a scale where an integer power lands exactly on `T`.

## Theorem 33 (sharpness of the moment bound) `[PROVED HERE]`
For `c = d_k^{(N)}` (the `k`-fold divisor function restricted to factors in `[N,2N]`),
```
   ∫_T^{2T}\Big|∑_{a∼N^{k}}c_a a^{-it}\Big|^2 dt
     = T∑_a|c_a|^2 + ∑_{a≠b}c_a\bar c_b\,O\!\big(\min(T,\ |\log(a/b)|^{-1})\big) ,
```
and since `|\log(a/b)| ≍ |a-b|/N^{k}` and the shifted convolution satisfies
`∑_a |c_ac_{a+h}| ≪ N^{k}T^{o(1)}` uniformly in `h`, the off-diagonal splits as
```
   T\!\!\sum_{0<|h|<N^k/T}\!\! N^kT^{o(1)} \;+\; N^k\!\!\sum_{h≥N^k/T}\!\!\frac{N^kT^{o(1)}}{h}
     \;=\; N^{2k}T^{o(1)} ,
```
so `∫|D_N^k|^2 ≍ (T + N^{k})N^{k}T^{o(1)}` — **the Montgomery–Vaughan bound is sharp, in both regimes.**
> **Consequence: the deficit `E_k(σ) − (2−2σ) = \frac{(2−2σ)(2σ−1)}{k+2−2σ}` of Cycle 34 cannot be

`RV^2 ≪ \|a\|_2^2\,\max_r ∑_s |K(t_r−t_s)|` with `K(u) = ∑_{n∼N}n^{iu}`, so

## The `k`-fold reflection exists — and gives nothing `[RECORDED DEAD END]`
The `k = 1` reflection that resolves `η ∈ [1/2,1)` is Poisson summation. Its `k`-fold analogue is the

***Both failures are consequences of the same fact — that `[N,2N]` is a set of integers and `τ`-fold
products of integers are integers only for integral `τ`. This is the precise algebraic content of the
Density Hypothesis, and it explains why every ANALYTIC substitute attempted in Cycles 177–259 (Hölder,

deficit: they replace an identity by an inequality, and the identity is arithmetic.*** ∎
> ### The two candidate repairs, and their status
> ```
>   (a) Fractional divisor coefficients.  d_τ(n) is defined for all real τ>0 via ζ(s)^{τ}, satisfies
>       \sum_{n ≤ x}d_τ(n)^{2} ≪ x(\log x)^{τ^{2}-1}, and IS divisor-bounded.  But D_a^{τ} is not

>       expand around, and a is supported away from n=1, so no such expansion exists.
>       ⟹ CLOSED: the fractional power of a Dirichlet polynomial without constant term is not a
>          Dirichlet series.
>   (b) Non-integer frequency mean value theorem.  For frequencies \{μ_j\} that are δ-separated,
>       \sum_r|\sum_jc_je^{-iμ_jt_r}|^{2} ≤ (T+δ^{-1})\sum_j|c_j|^{2}.  For D_a^{τ} the μ_j are τ-fold
>       sums of \log n, whose separation can be as small as N^{-τ\cdot\text{(anything)}}.
>       ⟹ CLOSED unless the frequency set is shown to be separated, which is a statement about
>          simultaneous Diophantine approximation of \{\log n\} — and by Lemma 245 the \log n of
>          integers of height ≤ H span a ℚ-space of dimension ≫ log H/loglog H, so their τ-fold sums
>          are dense on the scale required.
> ```
> ***So both repairs are closed, and the closure is arithmetic in each case. `OPEN CORE 305` is

> interpolation from its integer cases.***

real `τ∈(1,3/2]`.** Equivalently: **find a substitute for `D_a^{τ}`.** The natural candidates are

are `d_τ(n) = \binom{τ}{\ldots}`-type and still `N^{o(1)}`-bounded — the divisor function `d_τ` is
defined for all real `τ>0` and satisfies `\sum_{n≤x}d_τ(n)^{2} ≪ x(\log x)^{τ^{2}-1}`; (b) a
`τ`-fold multiplicative convolution with fractional multiplicity. **Candidate (a) is concrete: if
`D_a(t)^{τ}` can be given meaning as a Dirichlet series with coefficients bounded by `d_τ ≪ N^{o(1)}`
on the relevant range, the mean value theorem applies verbatim and the Density Hypothesis follows.
The obstruction is that `D_a^{τ}` is multivalued and its Dirichlet coefficients need not be small when
`D_a` has zeros — which is exactly where the large values are not.**

# Li Reciprocal Chebyshev Kernel

- **ID:** li-reciprocal-chebyshev-kernel
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (paper)
- **Source:** `docs/consolidated/gpt/research-topics.md` topic 20; `docs/consolidated/gpt/proof-route.md`
- **Statement:** Under FE folding, each Li coefficient is an exact Chebyshev-kernel transform of the reciprocal seam atoms `y=-(rho-1/2)^(-2)`; in the reciprocal moment chart this is an infinite shifted-moment expansion, not a finite triangular transform.

## Goal

Close a missing atlas edge between the Li chart and the corrected reciprocal-seam square-test chart. The Li coefficients are finite triangular in the ordinary `rho^{-k}` power sums, but after passing to the FE-folded reciprocal coordinate `y`, the chart change is a rational Chebyshev kernel whose Taylor expansion uses all shifted reciprocal moments.

## Gates

- [x] 0 -> 1 in-progress: well-posed, source-pure, attack idea
- [x] 1 -> 2 fully-proven: complete paper proof, `[PROVED HERE]`, no open dependency
- [x] 2 -> 3 formalized: **DONE (2026-08-16)** — `GaloisForLFunctions.liPairKernel_eq_chebyshev`,
  `hasSum_liChebyshevKernel_one`, `tsum_liChebyshevKernel_one` in
  `formal/GaloisForLFunctions/RHTower/LiReciprocalChebyshevKernel.lean`; `lake build` green; axiom
  footprint `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`
- [ ] 3 -> 4 publication-ready: standalone note if needed

## Proof

[PROVED HERE]

Let

```text
rho = 1/2 + w,
rho' = 1-rho = 1/2 - w
```

be an FE pair, and set

```text
y = -w^(-2).
```

The pair contribution to Li's coefficient is

```text
L_n(w) =
[1 - (1 - 1/rho)^n] + [1 - (1 - 1/rho')^n].
```

Put

```text
q = 1 - 1/rho = (w-1/2)/(w+1/2).
```

For the FE partner, `1 - 1/rho' = q^(-1)`. Hence

```text
L_n = 2 - (q^n + q^(-n)).
```

A direct calculation gives

```text
(q + q^(-1))/2 = (4-y)/(4+y).
```

Therefore, if `C_n` denotes the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind,

```text
L_n(y) = 2 - 2 C_n((4-y)/(4+y)).
```

This is an exact FE-folded Li kernel in the reciprocal seam coordinate.

Since `L_n(0)=0`, its Taylor expansion at the reciprocal accumulation point has the form

```text
L_n(y) = sum_{k>=1} c_{n,k} y^k.
```

The Taylor expansion is valid whenever the reciprocal atoms lie in `|y|<4`; for the `xi` divisor this follows from the standard verified zero-free region below the first nontrivial zero height, so `|rho-1/2|>1/2` for every nontrivial zero. Thus

```text
lambda_n = sum_{k>=1} c_{n,k} T_k,
qquad
T_k = sum_rho m_rho y_rho^k,
```

with absolute convergence. In particular, the Li-to-reciprocal chart is not finite triangular in the `T_k`; every `lambda_n` sees an infinite tail of reciprocal moments through a fixed rational kernel.

The first kernel begins

```text
L_1(y) = y - y^2/4 + y^3/16 - y^4/64 + ...
```

and higher `n` have the same singularity at `y=-4`, with coefficients decaying geometrically up to polynomial factors in `k`.

## Computation

Symbolic verification for `n=1..7` and coefficient extraction are archived in:

- `computations/2026-06-21-conway-li-reciprocal-chebyshev-kernel.py`
- `computations/2026-06-21-conway-li-reciprocal-chebyshev-kernel.txt`

## Route Consequence

The Li chart is a smoothed/global kernel chart over the reciprocal seam moments. A finite Li prefix cannot be treated as a finite shifted-Hankel prefix in disguise: it mixes all `T_k`. Conversely, any theorem deriving shifted square-test positivity from Li data must control this infinite Chebyshev kernel and cannot rely only on the known finite triangular `lambda_n <-> P_k` transform.

This makes the atlas edge explicit:

```text
ordinary power sums P_k  <--finite triangular-->  lambda_n,
reciprocal moments T_k   <--infinite Chebyshev kernel-->  lambda_n.
```

/-
# φ_b transcendence over ℂ(z) — the Mahler-method lane

The card's `u₀ ⟂ φ_b` proof cites Becker–Bergweiler for the `deg_U = 0` case: `φ_b` is **not**
algebraic over `ℂ(z)` for nonexceptional `b`. The natural-boundary route to this (φ_b's Julia set is a
natural boundary) is blocked: the Böttcher coordinate `bottcherCoord` is only built on the escape region
`escapeOpen c = {|z| > max(2,‖c‖)}`, not yet extended through the basin to `J_c`. The **Mahler-method**
route uses only the escape-region functional equation `φ_c(z²+c) = φ_c(z)²` (`bottcherCoord_quadratic`),
which IS available.

This file lays the Mahler groundwork. The transformation is `σ : z ↦ z²+c = quadratic c z`, a degree-`2`
self-map of the escape region; `φ_c` intertwines it with `w ↦ w²`. A polynomial relation
`P(z, φ_c(z)) = 0` therefore propagates: `P(σz, φ_c(z)²) = 0`. Iterating `σ` blows up the `z`-degree
geometrically while algebraicity bounds it — the Mahler/Nishioka contradiction (the remaining core).

* `quadratic_mem_escapeOpen` — `σ` preserves the escape region (strict expansion).
* `relation_propagate` — the functional-equation propagation of a relation under one application of `σ`.
* `relation_propagate_iterate` — its `n`-fold iterate: `P` evaluated at `(σⁿ z, φ_c(z)^{2ⁿ})` vanishes.
-/
import GaloisForLFunctions.Bottcher.BottcherCoord
import GaloisForLFunctions.Bottcher.Dynamics

open Polynomial Bottcher

namespace PhiMahler

/-- **The squaring map preserves the escape region.** If `z ∈ escapeOpen c` then `quadratic c z =
z²+c ∈ escapeOpen c`, by strict expansion `‖z‖ < ‖z²+c‖` beyond radius `2`. So `σ : z ↦ z²+c` is a
self-map of the domain on which `φ_c` is defined — the Mahler transformation. -/
@[aesop safe]
theorem quadratic_mem_escapeOpen {c z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ escapeOpen c) :
    quadratic c z ∈ escapeOpen c := by
  obtain ⟨hc, h2⟩ := mem_escapeOpen_regime hz
  exact lt_trans hz (quadratic_norm_lt hc h2)

/-- **`σⁿ` preserves the escape region.** Iterating `quadratic_mem_escapeOpen`. -/
@[aesop safe]
theorem quadratic_iterate_mem_escapeOpen {c z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ escapeOpen c) (n : ℕ) :
    (quadratic c)^[n] z ∈ escapeOpen c := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa using hz
  | succ k ih => rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply']; exact quadratic_mem_escapeOpen ih

/-- **Functional-equation propagation of a polynomial relation (one Mahler step).** If `P ∈ ℂ[z][Y]`
satisfies `P(z, φ_c(z)) = 0` throughout the escape region, then `P(σz, φ_c(z)²) = 0` there too, where
`σz = z²+c`. Proof: `σz ∈ escapeOpen c` (stability), so the relation holds at `σz`:
`P(σz, φ_c(σz)) = 0`; and `φ_c(σz) = φ_c(z)²` (`bottcherCoord_quadratic`). This is the algebraic shadow of
the dynamical conjugacy `φ_c ∘ f_c = (·)² ∘ φ_c`. -/
@[aesop safe]
theorem relation_propagate {c : ℂ} (P : Polynomial (Polynomial ℂ))
    (hrel : ∀ z ∈ escapeOpen c, P.eval₂ (evalRingHom z) (bottcherCoord c z) = 0)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ escapeOpen c) :
    P.eval₂ (evalRingHom (quadratic c z)) ((bottcherCoord c z) ^ 2) = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨hc, h2⟩ := mem_escapeOpen_regime hz
  have hq := hrel (quadratic c z) (quadratic_mem_escapeOpen hz)
  rwa [bottcherCoord_quadratic hc h2] at hq

/-- **`n`-fold Mahler propagation.** `P(σⁿ z, φ_c(z)^{2ⁿ}) = 0` on the escape region: the relation at
`σⁿ z` together with the iterated functional equation `φ_c(σⁿ z) = φ_c(z)^{2ⁿ}`. The `z`-degree of the
left coordinate grows like `2ⁿ` under `σⁿ`, while `Y` is replaced by `φ_c(z)^{2ⁿ}` — the geometric
blow-up that, against the fixed algebraic degree of a relation, drives the Mahler/Nishioka contradiction. -/
@[aesop safe]
theorem relation_propagate_iterate {c : ℂ} (P : Polynomial (Polynomial ℂ))
    (hrel : ∀ z ∈ escapeOpen c, P.eval₂ (evalRingHom z) (bottcherCoord c z) = 0)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ escapeOpen c) (n : ℕ) :
    P.eval₂ (evalRingHom ((quadratic c)^[n] z)) ((bottcherCoord c z) ^ (2 ^ n)) = 0 := by
  have hbott : bottcherCoord c ((quadratic c)^[n] z) = (bottcherCoord c z) ^ (2 ^ n) := by
    induction n with
    | zero => simp
    | succ k ih =>
      obtain ⟨hc, h2⟩ := mem_escapeOpen_regime (quadratic_iterate_mem_escapeOpen hz k)
      rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', bottcherCoord_quadratic hc h2, ih, ← pow_mul, pow_succ]
  have hq := hrel ((quadratic c)^[n] z) (quadratic_iterate_mem_escapeOpen hz n)
  rwa [hbott] at hq

/-- **The Mahler tower of roots.** Fix `z₀` in the escape region and set `w = φ_c(z₀)`. For every `n`,
`w^{2ⁿ}` is a root of the specialized one-variable polynomial `P(σⁿz₀, ·) = P.map (evalRingHom (σⁿz₀))`.
So a single point `z₀` produces an infinite sequence of roots `w, w², w⁴, …` of the family `P(σⁿz₀, ·)`
of *bounded* `Y`-degree `≤ deg_Y P`, with `|w^{2ⁿ}| = |w|^{2ⁿ}` blowing up when `|w|>1` (which holds on
the escape region, `|φ_c|=exp G>1`). This bounded-degree-vs-blow-up tension is the lever of the
Mahler/Nishioka contradiction; the remaining core is the precise height estimate that closes it. -/
@[aesop safe]

/-- Clean up the normal form into a more human-friendly format. This does everything
  `RingNF.cleanup` does and also pulls the scalar multiplication from the end of of each term to
  the start. i.e. x * y * (r • 1) → r • (x * y)
  Used by `cleanup`. -/
def cleanupSMul (cfg : RingNF.Config) (r : Simp.Result) : MetaM Simp.Result := do
  let thms : SimpTheorems := {}
  let thms ← [``add_zero, ``add_assoc_rev, ``_root_.mul_one, ``mul_assoc_rev, ``_root_.pow_one,
    ``mul_neg, ``add_neg, ``one_smul, ``mul_smul_comm, ``Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one
    ].foldlM (·.addConst ·) thms
  let thms ← [``nat_rawCast_0, ``nat_rawCast_1, ``nat_rawCast_2, ``int_rawCast_neg,
      ``nnrat_rawCast, ``rat_rawCast_neg].foldlM (·.addConst · (post := false)) thms
  let ctx ← Simp.mkContext { zetaDelta := cfg.zetaDelta }
    (simpTheorems := #[thms])
    (congrTheorems := ← getSimpCongrTheorems)
  pure <| ←
    r.mkEqTrans (← Simp.main r.expr ctx (methods := Lean.Meta.Simp.mkDefaultMethodsCore {})).1

/-- Turn scalar multiplication by an explicit constant in `R` into multiplication in `A`.

e.g. `(4 : ℚ) • x` becomes `4 * x` but `↑n • x` stays `↑n • x`.
-/
def cleanupConsts (cfg : RingNF.Config) (r : Simp.Result) : MetaM Simp.Result := do
  let thms : SimpTheorems := {}
  let thms ← [``add_zero, ``_root_.one_mul, ``_root_.mul_one,
    ``neg_mul, ``add_neg].foldlM (·.addConst ·) thms
  let thms ← [``ofNat_smul, ``neg_ofNat_smul, ``neg_1_smul, ``nnRat_ofNat_smul_1,
    ``nnRat_ofNat_smul_2, ``rat_ofNat_smul_1, ``rat_ofNat_smul_2
    ].foldlM (·.addConst · (post := false)) thms
  let ctx ← Simp.mkContext { zetaDelta := cfg.zetaDelta }
    (simpTheorems := #[thms])
    (congrTheorems := ← getSimpCongrTheorems)
  pure <| ←
    r.mkEqTrans (← Simp.main r.expr ctx (methods := Lean.Meta.Simp.mkDefaultMethodsCore {})).1

/-- The core of `algebra_nf with R` - normalize the expression `e` over the base ring `R`
Also used internally in `polynomial_nf`. -/
meta def evalExpr {u : Lean.Level} (R : Q(Type u)) (e : Expr) : AtomM Simp.Result := do
  let e ← withReducible <| whnf e
  guard e.isApp -- all interesting ring expressions are applications
  let ⟨v, A, e⟩ ← inferTypeQ' e
  let sA ← synthInstanceQ q(CommSemiring $A)
  let sR ← synthInstanceQ q(CommSemiring $R)
  let sAlg ← synthInstanceQ q(Algebra $R $A)
  let cr ← Algebra.mkCache sR
  let ca ← Algebra.mkCache sA
  assumeInstancesCommute
  let ⟨a, _, pa⟩ ← match
    ← Common.isAtomOrDerivable (Algebra.ringCompute q($sAlg) cr ca) ca.toCache q($e) with
    -- `none` indicates that `eval` will find something algebraic.
  | none => Common.eval rcℕ (Algebra.ringCompute sAlg cr ca) ca.toCache e
  | some none => failure -- No point rewriting atoms
  | some (some r) => pure r -- Nothing algebraic for `eval` to use, but `norm_num` simplifies.
  pure { expr := a, proof? := pa }

end Mathlib.Tactic.Algebra

ial def saturateCore (rs : LocalRuleSet) (goal : MVarId) : SaturateM MVarId :=
  withExceptionPrefix "saturate: internal error: " do
  goal.withContext do
    goal.checkNotAssigned `saturate
    let mut queue := ∅
    let (fs, ruleMatches) ← rs.mkInitialForwardState goal
    for m in ruleMatches do
      queue := queue.insert m
    let (fs, ruleMatches) ← fs.update goal (phase? := none)
    for m in ruleMatches do
      queue := queue.insert m
    go ∅ fs queue ∅ goal
where
  go (hypDepths : Std.HashMap FVarId Nat) (fs : ForwardState) (queue : Queue)
      (erasedHyps : Std.HashSet FVarId) (goal : MVarId) : SaturateM MVarId := do
    withIncRecDepth do
    checkSystem "saturate"
    goal.withContext do
      if let some (m, queue) := queue.deleteMin then
        if m.rule.name.phase == .unsafe || m.anyHyp erasedHyps.contains then
          return ← go hypDepths fs queue erasedHyps goal
        trace[saturate] "goal:{indentD goal}"
        let some (goal, hyp, removedHyps) ← profilingRule m.rule.name (·.isSome) do
          m.apply goal (skipExistingProps := true)
          | return ← go hypDepths fs queue erasedHyps goal
        goal.withContext do
          -- TODO use applyGoalDiff
          let fs ← profilingForwardState do
            return removedHyps.foldl (init := fs) λ fs h => fs.eraseHyp h
          let type ← hyp.getType
          let erasedHyps := erasedHyps.insertMany removedHyps
          let mut depth := 0
          let mut hypDepths := hypDepths
          let maxDepth? := (← read).options.forwardMaxDepth?
          if maxDepth?.isSome then
            depth := 1 + m.foldHyps (init := 0) λ depth h =>
              max depth (hypDepths[h]?.getD 0)
            hypDepths := hypDepths.insert hyp depth
          trace[saturate] "added hyp (depth {depth}) {Expr.fvar hyp} : {type}"
          if maxDepth?.isSome && depth ≥ maxDepth?.get! then
            go hypDepths fs queue erasedHyps goal
          else
            let rules ← profilingRuleSelection do
              rs.applicableForwardRules type
            let fs ← profilingForwardState do
              let patInsts ←
                rs.forwardRulePatternSubstsInLocalDecl (← hyp.getDecl)
              return fs.enqueueHypWithPatSubsts hyp rules patInsts
            let (fs, ruleMatches) ← fs.update goal (phase? := none)
            let queue :=
              ruleMatches.foldl (init := queue) λ queue m => queue.insert m
            go hypDepths fs queue erasedHyps goal
      else
        return goal

end Stateful

def saturateMain' (rs : LocalRuleSet) (goal : MVarId) : SaturateM MVarId :=
  profiling (fun stats _ total => { stats with total }) do
  let preState ← show MetaM _ from saveState
  let tacticState ←
    if (← read).options.generateScript then
      profiling (fun stats _ n => { stats with script := stats.script + n }) do
      Script.TacticState.mkInitial goal
    else
      pure default -- unused when script generation is disabled
  let preGoal := goal
  let goal ← profiling (fun stats _ search => { stats with search }) do
    if aesop.dev.statefulForward.get (← getOptions) then
      Stateful.saturateCore rs goal
    else
      saturateCore rs goal
  if (← read).options.generateScript then
    let steps ← get
    let tacticSeq ← profiling (fun stats _ n => { stats with script := stats.script + n }) do
      let uscript : Script.UScript ← steps.mapM (·.toStep)
      `(tacticSeq| $(← uscript.render tacticState):tactic*)
    recordScriptGenerated { method := .static, perfect := true, hasMVar := false }
    checkRenderedScriptIfEnabled tacticSeq preState preGoal
      (expectCompleteProof := false)
    if (← read).options.traceScript then
      addTryThisTacticSeqSuggestion (← getRef) tacticSeq
  return goal

def saturateMain (rs : LocalRuleSet) (goal : MVarId) : SaturateM MVarId := do
  let goal ← saturateMain' rs goal
  (← getStats).trace .stats
  return goal

def saturate (rs : LocalRuleSet) (goal : MVarId) (options : Aesop.Options') :
    MetaM (MVarId × Stats) := do
  saturateMain rs goal |>.run options

/-!
### Factorial via binary splitting.

We prove this is equal to the standard factorial and mark it `@[csimp]`.

We could proceed further, with either Legendre or Luschny methods.
-/

/-!
This is the highest factorial I can `#eval` using the naive implementation without a stack overflow:
```
/-- info: 114716 -/
#guard_msgs in
#eval 9718 ! |>.log2
```

Similarly, evaluation of `ascFactorial 100 15000` fails with the naive implementation
but works with the binary recursion.

We could implement a tail-recursive version (or just use `Nat.fold`),
but instead let's jump straight to binary splitting.
-/

/-- `ascFactorial` implemented using binary splitting.

While this still performs the same number of multiplications,
the big-integer operands to each are much smaller. -/
def ascFactorialBinary (n k : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  match k with
  | 0 => 1
  | 1 => n
  | k@(_ + 2) => ascFactorialBinary n (k / 2) * ascFactorialBinary (n + k / 2) ((k + 1) / 2)

@[csimp]
lemma ascFactorial_eq_ascFactorialBinary : ascFactorial = ascFactorialBinary := by
  ext n k
  fun_induction ascFactorialBinary with
  | case1 => simp
  | case2 => simp [ascFactorial]
  | case3 n k ih₁ ih₂ => grind [ascFactorial_mul_ascFactorial]

/-- Factorial implemented using binary splitting.

While this still performs the same number of multiplications,
the big-integer operands to each are much smaller. -/
def factorialBinarySplitting (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ascFactorialBinary 1 n

@[csimp]
theorem factorial_eq_factorialBinarySplitting : @factorial = @factorialBinarySplitting := by
  ext n
  simp [factorialBinarySplitting, ← ascFactorial_eq_ascFactorialBinary]

/-- `descFactorial` implemented using binary splitting. -/
def descFactorialBinary (n k : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n < k then 0
  else ascFactorialBinary (n - k + 1) k

@[csimp]
theorem descFactorial_eq_descFactorialBinary : descFactorial = descFactorialBinary := by
  ext n k
  rw [descFactorialBinary]
  split_ifs with h
  · rw [descFactorial_of_lt h]
  · rw [← ascFactorial_eq_ascFactorialBinary, ← add_descFactorial_eq_ascFactorial']
    grind

/-- Reciprocal exponential radius of the reflected logarithmic action. -/
def thetaCuspReflectedActionInverseRadius (u t : ℝ) : ℝ :=

/-- Reflected execution balance selects the central source tilt and only that tilt. -/
theorem symmetricSourceTiltMean_reflection_gap_eq_zero_iff {g : ℝ → ℝ} {x : ℝ}
    (hx : 0 < x) (hg : g (-x) < g x) (a : ℝ) :
    symmetricSourceTiltMean g a x - symmetricSourceTiltMean g (-a) x = 0 ↔ a = 0 := by

  · intro h
    by_contra ha
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne ha with ha | ha
    · have hp := symmetricSourceTiltMean_reflection_gap_pos (g := g) (a := -a) (x := x)
          (neg_pos.mpr ha) hx hg
      rw [neg_neg] at hp
      linarith
    · exact (ne_of_gt (symmetricSourceTiltMean_reflection_gap_pos ha hx hg)) h
  · rintro rfl
    simp

/-- Linear-entropy balance of a two-point even theta fibre selects the centre. -/
theorem thetaHasseExecutionTV_balance_eq_zero_iff {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) (a : ℝ) :

    (strictMono_thetaHasseExecutionTV (neg_lt_self hx)) a

    symmetricSourceTiltMean (fun y => geometricExecutionEntropy (thetaHasseRatio y)) a x -

/-- Mean in a finite weighted source fibre. -/
def finiteWeightedMean {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (w f : ι → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, w i * f i

/-- Variance in a finite weighted source fibre. -/
def finiteWeightedVariance {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (w f : ι → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, w i * (f i - finiteWeightedMean w f) ^ 2

/-- Covariance in a finite weighted source fibre. -/
def finiteWeightedCovariance {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (w f g : ι → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i, w i * (f i - finiteWeightedMean w f) * (g i - finiteWeightedMean w g)

/-- Finite Fisher-response law: every execution response is bounded by source variance times
statistic variance.  No probability normalization is needed for this weighted Cauchy--Schwarz
form; nonnegative weights are sufficient. -/
theorem finiteWeightedCovariance_sq_le_variance_mul_variance
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {w f g : ι → ℝ} (hw : ∀ i, 0 ≤ w i) :
    finiteWeightedCovariance w f g ^ 2 ≤
      finiteWeightedVariance w f * finiteWeightedVariance w g := by
  unfold finiteWeightedCovariance finiteWeightedVariance
  apply Finset.sum_sq_le_sum_mul_sum_of_sq_le_mul Finset.univ
  · intro i hi
    exact mul_nonneg (hw i) (sq_nonneg _)
  · intro i hi
    exact mul_nonneg (hw i) (sq_nonneg _)
  · intro i hi
    ring_nf
    exact le_rfl

end

source_arguments.statement:
theorem exists_nonzero_mixed_prefix_initial (S : Finset ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℂ)
    (hS : ∀ p ∈ S, 0<p) (hc : ∃ p ∈ S, c p≠0)
    (M : ℕ) (hM : ∀ p ∈ S, p≤M) (s : ℂ) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, n≤M ∧ endpoint (mixedPath S c s) (n+1)≠0
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem exists_nonzero_mixed_prefix_initial (S : Finset ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℂ)
    (hS : ∀ p ∈ S, 0<p) (hc : ∃ p ∈ S, c p≠0)
    (M : ℕ) (hM : ∀ p ∈ S, p≤M) (s : ℂ) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, n≤M ∧ endpoint (mixedPath S c s) (n+1)≠0
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  by_contra hn
  push Not at hn
  have hpref : ∀ N : ℕ, N≤M+1 → endpoint (mixedPath S c s) N=0 := by
    intro N hN
    cases N with
    | zero => simp [endpoint]
    | succ n => exact hn n (by omega)
  have hpath (n : ℕ) (hnM : n≤M) : mixedPath S c s n=0 := by
    have he := Finset.sum_range_succ (mixedPath S c s) n
    change endpoint (mixedPath S c s) (n+1)=endpoint (mixedPath S c s) n+mixedPath S c s n at he
    rw [hpref (n+1) (by omega), hpref n (by omega), zero_add] at he
    exact he.symm
  have hcoeff (n : ℕ) (hnM : n≤M) : ∑ p ∈ S, c p*eulerDeletionDirichletCoefficient p n=0 := by
    have he : mixedPath S c s n =
        (∑ p ∈ S, c p*eulerDeletionDirichletCoefficient p n)*kernel s n := by
      simp only [mixedPath, eulerDeletionWeightedJump, kernel, Finset.sum_mul]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro p hp
      ring
    have hk : kernel s n≠0 := by
      apply Complex.cpow_ne_zero_iff.mpr
      left
      have hx : 0<(n:ℝ)+1 := by positivity
      exact_mod_cast hx.ne'
    have h := hpath n hnM
    rw [he] at h
    exact (mul_eq_zero.mp h).resolve_right hk
  obtain ⟨p,hp,hcp⟩ := hc
  exact hcp (deletion_coefficients_independent_initial S c hS M hM hcoeff p hp)

# Perfect-return connected-path rigidity

- **ID:** perfect-return-connected-path-rigidity
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** CANDIDATE
- **Source:** positive survivor of the disconnected \(p=1\) locality objection

## Exact frontier

- `[CORPUS]` `one_fixed_nearestNeighbor_chain_every_future_probability`
  constructs a tridiagonal representative for every terminal probability
  in \([0,1]\). At \(p=1\), it is an active Krylov block plus a diagonal
  spectator block.
- `[LITERATURE]` For a finite irreducible Jacobi matrix, every eigenvector
  has nonzero first and last coordinate; equivalently, an endpoint basis
  vector is cyclic. This follows directly from the three-term recurrence
  and is classical; see Leite--Saldanha--Tomei,
  [*Reconstruction of tridiagonal matrices from spectral
  data*](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0508099).
- `[BRIDGE]` Applying endpoint cyclicity to the parity-supported perfect
  return state has not yet been made explicit in the local recurrence law.
  The classical Jacobi fact alone is not new scientific knowledge.

## Conjecture and hostile attack

`[CONJECTURE]` Let \(D_T\) have the simple spectrum
\(\{\pi j/T:0\leq j\leq 2q+1\}\), let \(e_0\) be the fixed endpoint state,
and let \(Ue_0\) be the odd-parity clock state. For
\(K=U^*D_TU\), every tridiagonal realization has at least one zero
off-diagonal path coupling.

Potential failures:

1. Perfect return alone need not omit any spectral phase when all energies
   acquire the same phase. Here the fixed spectrum contains both phase
   parities and the specified endpoint state has exactly zero weight on
   every even spectral level.
2. A tridiagonal matrix may be connected with complex or signed
   off-diagonal entries. Endpoint cyclicity needs only nonzero forward
   entries, not positivity or reality.
3. Degenerate spectra can carry endpoint-orthogonal eigenvectors even for
   less rigid graph structures. Here the proof uses an explicit
   endpoint-orthogonal eigenvector, not simplicity as an unproved shortcut.

Verdict: `SURVIVES PRELIMINARY ATTACK` as a sharp application and
classification boundary; `REDISCOVERED` if presented as a new standalone
Jacobi theorem.

## Dependency-closed paper proof

Let \(A\) be any tridiagonal operator on the path basis
\(e_0,\ldots,e_n\), with every forward matrix element
\(\langle e_k,Ae_{k+1}\rangle\neq0\). Suppose \(Av=\lambda v\) and
\(\langle e_0,v\rangle=0\). Inductively assume the first \(k+1\)
coordinates of \(v\) vanish. In row \(k\), tridiagonality eliminates every
coordinate above \(k+1\), while the induction hypothesis eliminates all
coordinates at or below \(k\). The eigenvalue equation therefore reduces to
\[
  \langle e_k,Ae_{k+1}\rangle\langle e_{k+1},v\rangle=0.
\]
The forward matrix element is nonzero, so the next coordinate vanishes.
Thus every coordinate of \(v\) is zero. Contrapositively, a nonzero
endpoint-orthogonal eigenvector forces at least one zero path coupling.

Now take any unitary \(U\) sending the fixed state \(e_0\) to the
odd-parity endpoint clock. For any even spectral basis vector \(f_{2a}\),
\[
  v=U^*f_{2a}
\]
is nonzero and is an eigenvector of \(K=U^*D_TU\). Moreover,
\[
  \langle e_0,v\rangle
  =\langle Ue_0,f_{2a}\rangle=0
\]
because the parity endpoint clock has zero weight on all even spectral
levels. The contraposition therefore forces a zero path coupling in every
tridiagonal fixed-protocol realization.

`[PAPER-PROVED]` Proof uses no positivity, real-coupling or unproved
spectral theorem. It is stronger than needed because the endpoint
propagation lemma applies to arbitrary complex tridiagonal operators.

## Formal target

1. Define nonzero-forward-coupling path connectedness.
2. Prove endpoint propagation for an arbitrary tridiagonal eigenvector.
3. Prove its zero-coupling contraposition.
4. Instantiate it with an even spectral eigenvector transported through an
   arbitrary endpoint unitary.
5. Audit axioms and add the exact boundary to manuscript and hostile review.

# HB fixed-weight orbit Ward symmetry no-go

Status: failed/retired
Route: HB
Closed: 2026-08-28

## Proposed route

Use FE reflection, Schwarz conjugation, Stokes orientation, or a fixed real group character to
force universal vanishing of the four-sector HC16 Peierls orbit trace without adding a physical
stationarity theorem.

## Exact obstruction

HC17 classifies every fixed reflection-invariant pair weighting:

`WardIdentity(n,a,b) ↔ a+b=0 ∨ RiemannHypothesis`.

Symmetry alone supplies only the zero-total choice `b=-a`. That identity cancels identically for
every Xi zero, including tilted zeros, so it is RH-blind. Every nonzero-total choice, including all
positive physical averages, is not a formal symmetry consequence: its universal vanishing is
equivalent to RH.

## Positive survivor

The sharp survivor is the nonzero-total Ward endpoint. A gauge-fixed action or boundary theorem
that independently proves

`HBXiPeierlsFESchwarzFixedWeightWardIdentity n a b`

for one fixed pair with `a+b ≠ 0` proves RH. Equal positive weights `a=b=1` give the canonical
endpoint. This survivor is dependency-closed and formalized in
`ThetaCuspHawkingBMFESchwarzFixedWeightWardDichotomy.lean`.

## Lean status

- Formalized theorem: `hbXiPeierlsFESchwarzFixedWeightWardIdentity_iff`
- Nonzero-total endpoint: `hbXiPeierlsFESchwarzFixedWeightWardIdentity_iff_rh_of_sum_ne_zero`
- Positive endpoint: `hbXiPeierlsFESchwarzPositiveWeightWardIdentity_iff_rh`
- Blind cancellation: `hbXiPeierlsFESchwarzZeroTotalWardIdentity`
- Target build passed; axiom audit contains only Lean/mathlib foundational axioms

## No-go conclusion

Retire fixed-weight orbit symmetry as a source of useful stationarity. It either chooses a
zero-total, information-erasing character or assumes/proves the full missing RH content. Continue
only through a literal physical derivation of a nonzero-total Ward law.

# PW bounded pairwise-positive endpoint tomography

- **ID:** PW-B-PPK-ENDPOINT-TOMOGRAPHY
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (Lean)
- **Source:** `rh-current-frontier-map.md` (read-only) · PW-B source-producer burden
- **Statement:** Every bounded symmetric pairwise-positive countable PW grade kernel whose quadratic endpoint-winding response vanishes at every prescribed physical tomography scale is the zero kernel.

## Goal

Kill bounded positive countable matrix completion as a PW-B producer. Exact chain attacked:

`countable PW matrix dynamics -> endpoint-winding darkness -> PW partner balance -> shared Ward charge extinction -> RH`.

If proved, nonzero bounded PSD/Gram histories cannot hide from the literal physical endpoint channel. Any surviving matrix producer must be indefinite, unbounded/singular, or not governed by pointwise quadratic endpoint energy.

## Gates

- [x] 0 -> 1 in-progress: statement fixed by corpus; direct attack and falsifiers identified
- [x] 1 -> 2 fully-proven: complete paper proof, `[PROVED HERE]`, no open dependency
- [x] 2 -> 3 formalized: Lean theorem, target-only `lake build`, axiom audit
- [ ] 3 -> 4 publication-ready: standalone theorem/proof/Lean certificate

## Corpus basis

- `schwarzschildParikhWilczekBoundedPacketEndpointResponse_eq_zero_iff`: physical nodes recover every bounded scalar grade packet.
- `schwarzschildParikhWilczekInfiniteGradeDarkMatrix_energy_zero`: a nonzero countable PSD rank-one matrix is invisible to all three Borel moments.
- `schwarzschildParikhWilczekEndpointWinding_defeats_infiniteGradeDarkMatrix`: literal endpoint winding detects that one explicit dark kernel.
- `pairwiseNonnegativeKernel_row_eq_zero_of_symmetric_of_diagonal_eq_zero`: positivity makes a zero diagonal annihilate its full row.
- `tsum_sum_antidiagonal`: summable double series regroup by total grade.
- `natCast_succ_le_two_pow`: anti-diagonal cardinal growth is absorbed by dyadic rescaling.

## Theorem C1

Let `K : N -> N -> R` be symmetric, uniformly bounded, and `PairwiseNonnegativeKernel K`. Put

`a_K(n) = sum_{i=0}^n K(i,n-i)`

and at the corpus physical nodes `q_j = exp(-(j+1))`,

`E_K(j) = sum_n a_K(n) q_j^(n+2)`.

Then `(forall j, E_K(j)=0) iff K=0`.

## Attack

1. `|a_K(n)| <= (n+1)B`; hence `b_K(n)=a_K(n)/2^n` is bounded.
2. Since `2q_j` is a nonzero sequence in `(0,1)` tending to zero, endpoint darkness and scalar bounded power-series uniqueness force every `a_K(n)=0`.
3. Induct on `m`. In `a_K(2m)`, earlier zero diagonals annihilate their full rows by pairwise positivity and symmetry, leaving only `K(m,m)`; hence `K(m,m)=0` and row `m` vanishes.
4. All rows vanish, so `K=0`.

## Proof

**[PROVED HERE]** Choose `B >= 0` with `|K(i,j)| <= B`. For
`a(n)=sum_{i=0}^n K(i,n-i)`, the triangle inequality gives
`|a(n)| <= (n+1)B`. Since `n+1 <= 2^n`, `b(n)=a(n)/2^n` is bounded by `B`.

Let `q_j=exp(-(j+1))` and `r_j=2q_j`. Then `0<r_j<1`, `r_j -> 0`, and absolute
convergence permits

`E_K(j) = q_j^2 sum_n b(n) r_j^n`.

Thus `E_K(j)=0` for every `j` forces `sum_n b(n)r_j^n=0` for every `j`.
Bounded power-series uniqueness on a nonzero sequence tending to zero gives `b(n)=0`, hence
`a(n)=0`, for every `n`.

Induct on `m`. Assume rows `0,...,m-1` vanish. In

`0=a(2m)=sum_{i=0}^{2m} K(i,2m-i)`,

terms with `i<m` vanish by the induction hypothesis. If `i>m`, then `2m-i<m`, so symmetry and
the induction hypothesis again kill the term. Only `K(m,m)` remains; therefore `K(m,m)=0`.
Pairwise positivity plus symmetry makes a null diagonal annihilate the complete row, so row `m`
vanishes. Induction yields `K=0`. The converse is immediate. Boundedness also majorizes the literal
double endpoint series by a product of two geometric series; antidiagonal regrouping therefore
identifies it with `E_K` without conditional rearrangement.

## Falsifiers

- A bounded symmetric pairwise-positive nonzero kernel with all `E_K(j)=0`.
- Failure of the antidiagonal response to equal the literal absolutely convergent double endpoint energy.
- A physical-node rescaling outside the open unit disk.

## Novelty audit

- Internal: no matching theorem found by corpus research; existing results cover bounded scalar packets, entrywise-positive matrices, finite/sample boundary regularizations, and two explicit PSD dark matrices only.
- External: searches through 2026-08 found standard PSD-kernel factorization/diagonal uniqueness and
  standard Parikh--Wilczek tunneling/correlation papers, but no countable PW grade-kernel endpoint
  tomography or this no-go. Generic ingredients are classical; route-specific theorem is new.

## No-go closure

- **Exact killing theorem/mechanism:** all-scale physical endpoint darkness plus pairwise positivity
  recursively kills every diagonal and row.
- **Strongest positive survivor:** every nonzero bounded symmetric pairwise-positive history is
  detected at some prescribed physical endpoint scale.

## Formalized theorem chain

For every `a>0`, Suzuki's finite-part boundary term applied to the exponential source is

```text
-(1/2) exp(x) log(a^2-x^2).
```

Lean proves this term tends to `+infinity` at `a-`. Adding any residual with a finite left endpoint
limit preserves divergence, so the resulting kernel profile cannot equal `c exp(x)` throughout
`(-a,a)`.

The second chain formalizes all integer modes, not a finite truncation. For any complex Hilbert
basis indexed by `Z`, vanishing of every nonzero coordinate forces the vector to equal its zero
mode. Applied to the free-clock sampling points

```text
z_n=pi n/a+i,
```

Lean proves:

1. `z_n != i` for `n!=0`;
2. Suzuki's explicit free carrier vanishes at every `z_n`;
3. equality of a finite-shift Livsic carrier with the free carrier at `z_n`, with its
   Hermite--Biehler denominator nonzero, forces the source Fourier sample to vanish;
4. equality at all nonzero samples forces the weighted source to be a pure zero mode;
5. an identically vanishing reflected cross-tangent numerator likewise forces a pure zero mode;
6. a genuine nonzero source mode forces the cross-tangent numerator to be nonzero somewhere.

| **endpoint completeness of the split system**: one edge coupling seeing every ordered old pair makes the attached qubit see *every* ordered pair of split labels, for all small nonzero coupling | `eventually_forall_layerGerm_endpoint_ne_zero` |
| **endpoint completeness is an open condition** in any continuously varying eigenvector family | `eventually_forall_layerReducedTransition_ne_zero` |

The formalisation forced one clarification of the paper argument.  The reduced-transition entry at
the *unflipped* new index has vanishing first-order term, because the edge perturbation is purely
cross-layer; only the flipped entry moves at first order.  So the index flip is not a convenience
but the unique first-order channel, and the hypothesis `alpha_0 != beta_0` turns out to be
unnecessary: the same computation covers the same-level pairs too.

### What remains for Theorem A

The recursion of Lemma A1 is now a closed cycle of formal theorems:

```text
endpoint completeness at stage n

    --[ eventually_forall_layerGerm_endpoint_ne_zero ]-->  endpoint completeness at stage n+1

                                                              intersection with the dense
                                                              maximal-rank set of the parent card
```

with the base case `n = 2` (four levels) and the `D >= 3` quadratic-rate base already formal.

**The physical realisation is now formal too.**

# Source-horizontal Euler--Wold indefinite endpoint-annihilation firewall

- **ID:** `P-G210-IEA`
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** `[LEAN-PROVED] [NO-GO CLASSIFICATION] [POSITIVE SURVIVOR]`
- **Route:** Frankenstein P + Euler--Wold BV/Krein + bilateral prime-angle sewing
- **Statement:** Classify whether a source-budgeted order-indefinite block can cancel literal
  endpoint excess before scalar domination without destroying coefficient-faithful bilateral Xi
  admission.

## Goal

Previous module constructs a transverse reporter `T_N` with `0<T_N<P(c)` cofinally, while literal
endpoint response `R_N` satisfies `P(c)<R_N` cofinally.  Linear domination is therefore impossible.
This card tests remaining possibility: retain `R_N` as positive corner, cancel excess by negative
source leg before scalarization, then ask whether cancellation survives physical Xi admission.

## Frozen conjecture loop

### C0 -- unique signed counterleg

Put

```text
K_N = T_N - R_N,
S_N = diag(R_N,K_N).
```

Predictions:

1. `tr S_N=T_N` exactly;
2. among diagonal blocks with first corner `R_N` and trace `T_N`, second corner is uniquely `K_N`;
3. for every nonzero conormal, cofinally `R_N>0` and `K_N<0`, so cancellation is genuinely
   order-indefinite rather than disguised positive domination.

### C1 -- physical Krein rotation

Apply fundamental symmetry `J=diag(1,-1)`.  Prediction: C0 cancellation is not physical-order
stable:

```text
tr(J S_N)=2 R_N-T_N>P(c)
```

cofinally.  Thus `J` converts the negative counterleg to positive excess and amplifies, rather than
solves, primitive-budget overspend.

### C2 -- bilateral Hardy--Stokes reinterpretation

Scale both Hardy orientations for `lambda_p(rho)` by nonzero endpoint energy.  Predictions:

1. scaled sewing defects cancel identically before scalarization;
2. nonzero scalar multiplication preserves and reflects bilateral moderation;
3. both scaled orientations are moderate iff `Re rho=1/2`;
4. consequently every retained strict-right Xi copy has exact signed cancellation but cannot be
   admitted to the coefficient-faithful bilateral source topology.

## Hostile audit

- C0 is not an RH proof unless cancellation survives a physical source topology/order.  Trace zero
  or bounded trace alone is blind to positive corner.
- C1 explicitly tests this missing compatibility rather than assuming it.
- C2 forbids claiming that a scalar endpoint counterterm repairs off-line exponential Fourier
  growth: any nonzero scalar leaves moderation unchanged.
- Connes--Consani archimedean Sonin positivity and Connes--Consani--Moscovici semilocal stability
  provide compressed positive spaces, not this coefficient-faithful finite endpoint counterleg or
  a theorem placing both off-unitary Hardy halves in one moderate source topology.  Connes--Consani--
  Marcolli identify global trace-pairing positivity as RH-equivalent.  Therefore an unconditional
  physical positive descent cannot be imported from those results.

## Proof plan

1. Prove generic scalar-multiplication and sewing covariance lemmas for `bilateralModerate` and
   `bilateralSewing`.
2. Construct signed endpoint block and prove exact trace, uniqueness, eventual inertia, and
   physical-rotation overspend.
3. Attach literal endpoint scale to both Hardy halves.  Prove exact cancellation and sharp
   moderation criterion.
4. Specialize to actual Gamma--Julia Xi conormal coefficient and retain support-copy fidelity.
5. Formalize exact positive survivor/no-go; wire leaf into `RHTower.lean` without umbrella build.

## No-go closure

- **Exact killing mechanism:** The unique diagonal counterleg is `K_N=T_N-R_N`.  It is cofinally
  negative.  Fundamental-symmetry rotation changes signed trace `T_N` into `2R_N-T_N`, which
  cofinally exceeds primitive budget.  In prime-angle source topology, nonzero endpoint scaling
  preserves bilateral moderation exactly, so exact cancellation cannot admit an off-line Xi copy.
- **Strongest positive survivor:** Exact order-indefinite annihilation exists before scalarization:
  `tr diag(R_N,T_N-R_N)=T_N`, and endpoint-scaled Hardy--Stokes boundary defects cancel identically.
  Construction retains actual Gamma--Julia coefficient, both reflection orientations, and analytic

- **New insight:** Obstruction is not lack of signed cancellation.  It is incompatibility between
  signed cancellation and physical source admission.  Any further scalar/Krein endpoint correction

  orientations, or prove an independent full-source admission theorem.

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Sieve.MatomakiTeravainenHarmanBoundary
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.Sieve.MatomakiTeravainenMainLayerChains

/-!
# Exact rectangular cells for Harman pairs and triples

Distinct ordered aligned cells remove both prime-order predicates.  A cell whose upper pair
product lies below the Harman threshold removes the remaining coupled geometry predicate.  The
only tuples outside these literal rectangles are same-cell order collisions and the threshold
boundary fibre already estimated at paper scale.
-/

namespace RHTower.Sieve

open Finset

noncomputable section

/-- Ordered pair cells on which `q₂<q₁` and `q₁q₂⁴<E` hold uniformly. -/
def mtHarmanGoodPairCells {t : ℕ} (endpoint : ℕ → ℕ) (E : ℝ) :
    Finset (Fin t × Fin t) :=
  Finset.univ.filter fun cell =>
    cell.2.1 < cell.1.1 ∧
      mtAdjacentBlockUpperScale endpoint cell.1 *
        mtAdjacentBlockUpperScale endpoint cell.2 ^ 4 < E

theorem mem_mtHarmanGoodPairCells {t : ℕ} {endpoint : ℕ → ℕ} {E : ℝ}
    {i₁ i₂ : Fin t} :
    (i₁, i₂) ∈ mtHarmanGoodPairCells endpoint E ↔
      i₂.1 < i₁.1 ∧
        mtAdjacentBlockUpperScale endpoint i₁ *
          mtAdjacentBlockUpperScale endpoint i₂ ^ 4 < E := by
  simp [mtHarmanGoodPairCells]

/-- Ordered triple cells on which `q₃<q₂<q₁` and `q₁q₂⁴<E` hold uniformly. -/
def mtHarmanGoodTripleCells {t : ℕ} (endpoint : ℕ → ℕ) (E : ℝ) :
    Finset ((Fin t × Fin t) × Fin t) :=
  Finset.univ.filter fun cell =>
    cell.2.1 < cell.1.2.1 ∧ cell.1.2.1 < cell.1.1.1 ∧
      mtAdjacentBlockUpperScale endpoint cell.1.1 *
        mtAdjacentBlockUpperScale endpoint cell.1.2 ^ 4 < E

theorem mem_mtHarmanGoodTripleCells {t : ℕ} {endpoint : ℕ → ℕ} {E : ℝ}
    {i₁ i₂ i₃ : Fin t} :
    ((i₁, i₂), i₃) ∈ mtHarmanGoodTripleCells endpoint E ↔
      i₃.1 < i₂.1 ∧ i₂.1 < i₁.1 ∧
        mtAdjacentBlockUpperScale endpoint i₁ *
          mtAdjacentBlockUpperScale endpoint i₂ ^ 4 < E := by
  simp [mtHarmanGoodTripleCells]

/-- Every prime pair chosen from one good cell satisfies both coupled source predicates. -/
theorem mtHarmanGoodPairCell_order_geometry
    {t : ℕ} {endpoint : ℕ → ℕ}
    (hendpoint : ∀ i, 1 ≤ endpoint i) (hmono : Monotone endpoint)
    {E : ℝ} {i₁ i₂ : Fin t}
    (hcell : (i₁, i₂) ∈ mtHarmanGoodPairCells endpoint E)
    {q₁ q₂ : ℕ}
    (hq₁ : q₁ ∈ mtAdjacentPrimeBlock endpoint i₁)
    (hq₂ : q₂ ∈ mtAdjacentPrimeBlock endpoint i₂) :
    q₂ < q₁ ∧ (q₁ : ℝ) * (q₂ : ℝ) ^ 4 < E := by
  have hcell' := mem_mtHarmanGoodPairCells.mp hcell
  exact ⟨prime_lt_of_adjacentBlock_index_lt hmono hcell'.1 hq₁ hq₂,
    (adjacentBlock_product_le_upper hendpoint hq₁ hq₂).trans_lt hcell'.2⟩

/-- Every prime triple chosen from one good cell satisfies both prime orders and the coupled
source geometry. -/
theorem mtHarmanGoodTripleCell_orders_geometry
    {t : ℕ} {endpoint : ℕ → ℕ}
    (hendpoint : ∀ i, 1 ≤ endpoint i) (hmono : Monotone endpoint)
    {E : ℝ} {i₁ i₂ i₃ : Fin t}
    (hcell : ((i₁, i₂), i₃) ∈ mtHarmanGoodTripleCells endpoint E)
    {q₁ q₂ q₃ : ℕ}
    (hq₁ : q₁ ∈ mtAdjacentPrimeBlock endpoint i₁)
    (hq₂ : q₂ ∈ mtAdjacentPrimeBlock endpoint i₂)
    (hq₃ : q₃ ∈ mtAdjacentPrimeBlock endpoint i₃) :
    q₃ < q₂ ∧ q₂ < q₁ ∧ (q₁ : ℝ) * (q₂ : ℝ) ^ 4 < E := by
  have hcell' := mem_mtHarmanGoodTripleCells.mp hcell
  exact ⟨prime_lt_of_adjacentBlock_index_lt hmono hcell'.1 hq₂ hq₃,
    prime_lt_of_adjacentBlock_index_lt hmono hcell'.2.1 hq₁ hq₂,
    (adjacentBlock_product_le_upper hendpoint hq₁ hq₂).trans_lt hcell'.2.2⟩

/-- Nonempty good pair cells; these are exactly the pair rectangles that contribute a nonzero
piece. -/
def mtHarmanActiveGoodPairCells {t : ℕ} (endpoint : ℕ → ℕ) (E : ℝ) :
    Finset (Fin t × Fin t) :=
  (mtHarmanGoodPairCells endpoint E).filter fun cell =>
    (mtAdjacentPrimeBlock endpoint cell.1).Nonempty ∧
      (mtAdjacentPrimeBlock endpoint cell.2).Nonempty

theorem mem_mtHarmanActiveGoodPairCells
    {t : ℕ} {endpoint : ℕ → ℕ} {E : ℝ} {i₁ i₂ : Fin t} :
    (i₁, i₂) ∈ mtHarmanActiveGoodPairCells endpoint E ↔
      (i₁, i₂) ∈ mtHarmanGoodPairCells endpoint E ∧
        (mtAdjacentPrimeBlock endpoint i₁).Nonempty ∧
          (mtAdjacentPrimeBlock endpoint i₂).Nonempty := by
  simp [mtHarmanActiveGoodPairCells]

/-- Nonempty good triple cells; these are exactly the triple rectangles that contribute a nonzero
piece. -/
def mtHarmanActiveGoodTripleCells {t : ℕ} (endpoint : ℕ → ℕ) (E : ℝ) :
    Finset ((Fin t × Fin t) × Fin t) :=
  (mtHarmanGoodTripleCells endpoint E).filter fun cell =>
    (mtAdjacentPrimeBlock endpoint cell.1.1).Nonempty ∧
      (mtAdjacentPrimeBlock endpoint cell.1.2).Nonempty ∧
        (mtAdjacentPrimeBlock endpoint cell.2).Nonempty

theorem mem_mtHarmanActiveGoodTripleCells
    {t : ℕ} {endpoint : ℕ → ℕ} {E : ℝ} {i₁ i₂ i₃ : Fin t} :
    ((i₁, i₂), i₃) ∈ mtHarmanActiveGoodTripleCells endpoint E ↔
      ((i₁, i₂), i₃) ∈ mtHarmanGoodTripleCells endpoint E ∧
        (mtAdjacentPrimeBlock endpoint i₁).Nonempty ∧
          (mtAdjacentPrimeBlock endpoint i₂).Nonempty ∧

/-
# Theorem A from endpoint completeness alone

Endpoint completeness of an eigenvector family -- every ordered pair has nonzero reduced transition
-- already produces the transition channel the extension step needs: one Hermitian probe sees all
the pairs at once, and its channel in the eigenbasis is Hermitian with every off-diagonal entry
nonzero.  Feeding that into the extension step removes the channel from the hypotheses, leaving
only the two spectral conditions of the card: simple spectrum and distinct ordered gaps.

Main result:
* `exists_endpointComplete_extensionChart_quadraticOrbit_ne_zero` — **Theorem A at one extension
  step, from Lemma A1's output**.
-/
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.ExtensionStepQuadraticOrbit
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.HermitianCoveringProbe

open Matrix

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

/-- **Theorem A at one extension step, from endpoint completeness.**  An endpoint-complete
eigenvector family over a simple old spectrum with distinct ordered gaps produces a Hermitian
transition channel seeing every ordered pair, and hence a one-qubit extension chart on which no
nonzero zero-sum coefficient packet satisfies the quadratic-rate relation under any labeling. -/
theorem exists_endpointComplete_extensionChart_quadraticOrbit_ne_zero
    {A cc dd : Type*} [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A] [Nonempty A]
    [Fintype cc] [DecidableEq cc] [Fintype dd]
    (hcard : 3 ≤ Fintype.card A)
    {E : A → ℝ} (hE : Function.Injective fun a => (E a : ℂ))
    (hgap : ∀ α β γ δ : A, α ≠ β → γ ≠ δ →
      ((E β : ℂ) - (E α : ℂ)) = ((E δ : ℂ) - (E γ : ℂ)) → (α, β) = (γ, δ))
    (ψ : A → cc × dd → ℂ)
    (hne : ∀ i j : A, i ≠ j → reducedTransition (ψ i) (ψ j) ≠ 0)
    (c : A × Bool → ℂ) (κ : ℂ) (hzero : ∑ i, c i = 0) (hcne : c ≠ 0) :
    ∃ M : Matrix A A ℂ, M.IsHermitian ∧ (∀ α β : A, α ≠ β → M β α ≠ 0) ∧
      ∃ (z₀ : ℂ) (C : LocalExtensionEigenbranchChart (fun a => (E a : ℂ)) (boolShift z₀) M),
        ∃ p ∈ C.U, (∏ σ : Equiv.Perm (A × Bool),
          ((∑ i, c i * C.branch (σ i) p) ^ 2
            - κ * ((localExtensionMatrix (fun a => (E a : ℂ)) p.1 M p.2) ^ 2).trace)) ≠ 0 := by
  obtain ⟨X, hXherm, hX⟩ := exists_hermitian_covering_endpoint_probe ψ hne
  refine ⟨endpointChannel ψ X, isHermitian_endpointChannel ψ hXherm, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro α β hαβ
    exact endpointChannel_ne_zero ψ hX β α (Ne.symm hαβ)
  · exact exists_extensionChart_quadraticOrbit_ne_zero hcard hE hgap
      (isHermitian_endpointChannel ψ hXherm)
      (fun α β hαβ => endpointChannel_ne_zero ψ hX β α (Ne.symm hαβ)) c κ hzero hcne

end

end GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.EndpointProbeTransitionCriterion
import Mathlib.Algebra.MvPolynomial.Funext
import Mathlib.Data.Finset.Sym

/-!
# One probe that sees every transition

Endpoint completeness delivers, for each ordered pair of levels, *some* probe of a finite family
with a nonzero matrix element.  A single edge coupling, however, is one operator.  A generic
complex combination of the family works: each matrix element is a nonzero linear form in the
combination coefficients, the product of those forms over all ordered pairs is a nonzero
polynomial, and a nonzero polynomial over `ℂ` has a point where it does not vanish.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

noncomputable section

variable {S A : Type*} [Fintype S] [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A]

/-- The linear form recording one matrix element of a combination of probes. -/
def probeCombinationForm (M : S → Matrix A A ℂ) (α β : A) : MvPolynomial S ℂ :=
  ∑ s, MvPolynomial.C (M s α β) * MvPolynomial.X s

omit [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A] in
theorem eval_probeCombinationForm (M : S → Matrix A A ℂ) (α β : A) (t : S → ℂ) :
    MvPolynomial.eval t (probeCombinationForm M α β) = ∑ s, t s * M s α β := by
  simp only [probeCombinationForm, map_sum, MvPolynomial.eval_mul, MvPolynomial.eval_C,
    MvPolynomial.eval_X]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun s _ => by ring

omit [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A] in
theorem probeCombinationForm_ne_zero {M : S → Matrix A A ℂ} {α β : A}
    (h : ∃ s, M s α β ≠ 0) : probeCombinationForm M α β ≠ 0 := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨s₀, hs₀⟩ := h
  intro hzero
  have heval := congrArg (MvPolynomial.eval (fun s => if s = s₀ then (1 : ℂ) else 0)) hzero
  rw [eval_probeCombinationForm] at heval
  have hval : (∑ s, (if s = s₀ then (1 : ℂ) else 0) * M s α β) = M s₀ α β := by simp
  rw [hval] at heval
  simpa using hs₀ (by simpa using heval)

omit [DecidableEq A] in
/-- **A single probe that sees every ordered pair.**  A generic complex combination of a covering
probe family has every off-diagonal matrix element nonzero. -/
theorem exists_probeCombination_ne_zero (M : S → Matrix A A ℂ)
    (hcover : ∀ α β : A, α ≠ β → ∃ s, M s α β ≠ 0) :
    ∃ t : S → ℂ, ∀ α β : A, α ≠ β → (∑ s, t s • M s) α β ≠ 0 := by
  classical
  set Q : MvPolynomial S ℂ :=
    ∏ p ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset A).offDiag, probeCombinationForm M p.1 p.2 with hQ
  have hQne : Q ≠ 0 := by
    rw [hQ]
    refine Finset.prod_ne_zero_iff.mpr fun p hp => ?_
    have hne : p.1 ≠ p.2 := (Finset.mem_offDiag.mp hp).2.2
    exact probeCombinationForm_ne_zero (hcover p.1 p.2 hne)
  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ : ∃ t : S → ℂ, MvPolynomial.eval t Q ≠ 0 := by
    by_contra hcon
    simp only [not_exists, not_not] at hcon
    exact hQne (MvPolynomial.funext fun x => by simpa using hcon x)
  refine ⟨t, fun α β hαβ => ?_⟩
  have hmem : (α, β) ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset A).offDiag :=
    Finset.mem_offDiag.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ α, Finset.mem_univ β, hαβ⟩
  have hfac : MvPolynomial.eval t (probeCombinationForm M α β) ≠ 0 := by
    intro hz
    apply ht
    rw [hQ, map_prod]
    exact Finset.prod_eq_zero hmem hz
  rw [eval_probeCombinationForm] at hfac
  have hentry : (∑ s, t s • M s) α β = ∑ s, t s * M s α β := by
    rw [Matrix.sum_apply]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun s _ => by simp
  rw [hentry]
  exact hfac

/-! ## From endpoint completeness to one covering endpoint operator -/

variable {c d : Type*} [Fintype c] [DecidableEq c] [Fintype d]

omit [DecidableEq c] in
theorem endpointPairing_sum_probe {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (X : ι → Matrix c c ℂ) (t : ι → ℂ)
    (ψ φ : c × d → ℂ) :
    endpointPairing ψ (endpointProbeAction (∑ q, t q • X q) φ)
      = ∑ q, t q * endpointPairing ψ (endpointProbeAction (X q) φ) := by
  rw [endpointPairing_probe_eq_trace, Finset.sum_mul, Matrix.trace_sum]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun q _ => ?_

/-!
# The defect-slope normal form

On a one-dimensional differential module a single nonzero defect determines every other one: there
is exactly one slope `ρ` with `ε₂ = ρ ε₁`.  That is the whole of the normal-form construction; the
one-dimensionality is the geometric input and the nonvanishing is the defect-lattice input.

The accompanying regulator identity is branch bookkeeping.  Integrating `d log Y - dX` from `q` to
`p` gives `(L p - L q) - (X p - X q)` for the chosen logarithm branch `L`.  When the endpoint
satisfies `Y p = exp (X p)` the transcendental endpoint coordinate cancels and only the algebraic
base point survives, up to the branch integer:

`∫ = X q - L q + 2πi k`.
-/

open Module

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-! ## The slope is unique -/

variable {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]

/-- **The defect slope exists and is unique.**  On a one-dimensional module a nonzero element is a
basis, so every element is a unique multiple of it. -/
theorem existsUnique_defectSlope (hrank : finrank K V = 1) {ε₁ : V} (hε : ε₁ ≠ 0) (ε₂ : V) :
    ∃! ρ : K, ε₂ = ρ • ε₁ := by
  have hspan : (K ∙ ε₁) = ⊤ := (finrank_eq_one_iff_of_nonzero ε₁ hε).mp hrank
  have hmem : ε₂ ∈ (K ∙ ε₁) := by rw [hspan]; exact Submodule.mem_top
  obtain ⟨ρ, hρ⟩ := Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mp hmem
  refine ⟨ρ, hρ.symm, fun σ hσ => ?_⟩
  have hzero : (σ - ρ) • ε₁ = 0 := by
    rw [sub_smul, ← hσ, hρ, sub_self]
  rcases smul_eq_zero.mp hzero with h | h
  · exact sub_eq_zero.mp h
  · exact absurd h hε

/-- The slope of a nonzero defect against itself is one. -/
theorem defectSlope_self (hrank : finrank K V = 1) {ε₁ : V} (hε : ε₁ ≠ 0) :
    (existsUnique_defectSlope hrank hε ε₁).choose = 1 := by
  have h := (existsUnique_defectSlope hrank hε ε₁).choose_spec
  exact (h.2 1 (one_smul K ε₁).symm).symm

/-! ## The regulator identity -/

/-- **The regulator identity.**  If the endpoint value is the exponential of the endpoint
coordinate, then the endpoint coordinate cancels from `(L p - L q) - (X p - X q)` and only the base
point survives, up to a branch integer. -/
theorem regulator_eq_base_add_branch {Xp Xq Lp Lq : ℂ}
    (hbranch : Complex.exp Lp = Complex.exp Xp) :
    ∃ k : ℤ, (Lp - Lq) - (Xp - Xq) = Xq - Lq + (k : ℂ) * (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I) := by
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := Complex.exp_eq_exp_iff_exists_int.mp hbranch
  refine ⟨k, ?_⟩
  rw [hk]
  ring

/-- The branch integer is the only freedom: two logarithm branches at the same endpoint give
regulator values differing by an integer multiple of `2πi`. -/
theorem regulator_branch_difference {Lp Lp' Xq Lq Xp : ℂ}
    (h : Complex.exp Lp = Complex.exp Lp') :
    ∃ k : ℤ, ((Lp - Lq) - (Xp - Xq)) - ((Lp' - Lq) - (Xp - Xq))
      = (k : ℂ) * (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I) := by
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := Complex.exp_eq_exp_iff_exists_int.mp h
  refine ⟨k, ?_⟩
  rw [hk]
  ring

    linarith)

    ((xi_differentiable.analyticAt _).comp hb) hn).mul
      ((sourceSlope_differentiable (conj (q.1:ℂ))).analyticAt s)).mul
        ((sourceSlope_differentiable (q.1:ℂ)).analyticAt s)

private theorem xi_eq_half_mul_reflected {w : ℂ} (hw : 0 < w.re) (hw1 : w ≠ 1) :
    xi w = w*(w-1)/2 * reflectedCompletedLambda w := by
  have hw0 : w ≠ 0 := by intro he; simp [he] at hw
  rw [xi_eq_half_mul hw0 hw1, reflectedCompletedLambda, riemannZeta_def_of_ne_zero hw0]
  field_simp [Complex.Gammaℝ_ne_zero_of_re_pos hw]

private theorem scatteringRatio_eq_xi {s : ℂ} (hs : 1/2 < s.re) :
    reflectedCompletedLambda (2*s) / reflectedCompletedLambda (2*s+1) =
      ((2*s+1)/(2*s-1)) * (xi (2*s) / xi (2*s+1)) := by
  have h2 : 1 < (2*s).re := by norm_num [Complex.mul_re]; linarith
  have h3 : 1 < (2*s+1).re := by norm_num [Complex.add_re, Complex.mul_re]; linarith
  have hn2 : 2*s ≠ 1 := by intro h; norm_num [h] at h2
  have hn3 : 2*s+1 ≠ 1 := by intro h; norm_num [h] at h3
  have hz2 : 2*s ≠ 0 := by intro h; norm_num [h] at h2
  have hz3 : 2*s+1 ≠ 0 := by intro h; norm_num [h] at h3

/-!
# Sharp Laplace wall of the global critical prime-tail Green potential

The positive source behind the global Green potential has exact absolute-convergence abscissa
`1 / 2` in the shifted Laplace variable.  Sufficiency was used in the global Fubini theorem.
Necessity is forced already by ordinary primes: at the boundary their damped masses are exactly
`1 / p`.

This is the sharp obstruction to extending the raw positive-source/passive realization toward the
critical line.  Any continuation across this wall must use cancellation or a non-positive
renormalization; stronger majorants cannot move the wall.
-/

open Complex Filter Function MeasureTheory Set TopologicalSpace
open scoped BigOperators ENNReal Topology

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- Ordinary primes embedded as the first Euler layer of the Deninger prime-power comb. -/
def criticalPrimeTailPrimeIndex (p : Nat.Primes) : DeningerPrimePowerIndex :=
  deningerEulerPrimePowerIndex (p, 0)

theorem criticalPrimeTailPrimeIndex_injective :
    Function.Injective criticalPrimeTailPrimeIndex := by
  intro p q hpq
  have hpq' : (p, 0) = (q, 0) :=
    deningerEulerPrimePowerIndex_injective hpq
  exact congrArg Prod.fst hpq'

/-- Real positive Laplace mass of one critical source atom. -/
def criticalPrimeTailLaplaceMass (r : ℝ) (n : DeningerPrimePowerIndex) : ℝ :=
  criticalPrimeTailAtomWeight n *
    Real.exp (-(r * deningerPrimePowerTime n))

/-- On the first Euler layer, critical Laplace mass is the exact prime power
`p^(-(r+1/2))`. -/
theorem criticalPrimeTailLaplaceMass_prime (r : ℝ) (p : Nat.Primes) :
    criticalPrimeTailLaplaceMass r (criticalPrimeTailPrimeIndex p) =
      (p : ℝ) ^ (-(r + 1 / 2)) := by
  have hp0 : (0 : ℝ) < p := by exact_mod_cast p.property.pos
  have hp1 : (1 : ℝ) < p := by exact_mod_cast p.property.one_lt
  have hlog : Real.log (p : ℝ) ≠ 0 := (Real.log_pos hp1).ne'
  have hweight :
      criticalPrimeTailAtomWeight (criticalPrimeTailPrimeIndex p) =
        (p : ℝ) ^ (-(1 / 2 : ℝ)) := by
    rw [criticalPrimeTailAtomWeight, criticalMellinAtomWeight]
    simp only [criticalPrimeTailPrimeIndex, deningerEulerPrimePowerIndex,
      Nat.zero_add, Nat.pow_one, deningerPrimePowerTime,
      ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_apply_prime p.property]
    field_simp
  rw [criticalPrimeTailLaplaceMass, hweight]
  have htime : deningerPrimePowerTime (criticalPrimeTailPrimeIndex p) =
      Real.log (p : ℝ) := by
    simpa [criticalPrimeTailPrimeIndex] using
      deningerPrimePowerTime_euler (p, 0)
  rw [htime, Real.rpow_def_of_pos hp0, Real.rpow_def_of_pos hp0,
    ← Real.exp_add]
  congr 1
  ring

/-- At and left of the half-density wall, the positive Laplace source is not summable. -/
theorem not_summable_criticalPrimeTailLaplaceMass_of_le_half
    {r : ℝ} (hr : r ≤ 1 / 2) :
    ¬ Summable (criticalPrimeTailLaplaceMass r) := by
  intro hsum
  have hprime := hsum.comp_injective criticalPrimeTailPrimeIndex_injective
  have hpow : Summable (fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℝ) ^ (-(r + 1 / 2))) :=
    hprime.congr fun p => criticalPrimeTailLaplaceMass_prime r p
  exact not_summable_primeRpow_of_negOne_le (by linarith) hpow

/-- **C43 sharp wall.**  The full positive critical source has absolute Laplace abscissa exactly
`1/2`; this is an iff, not only a one-sided convergence estimate. -/
theorem summable_criticalPrimeTailLaplaceMass_iff (r : ℝ) :
    Summable (criticalPrimeTailLaplaceMass r) ↔ 1 / 2 < r := by
  constructor
  · intro hsum
    exact lt_of_not_ge fun hr =>
      not_summable_criticalPrimeTailLaplaceMass_of_le_half hr hsum
  · intro hr
    exact summable_criticalPrimeTailAtomWeight_mul_exp_neg hr

/-- Complex Laplace atoms have the same exact absolute-convergence wall. -/
theorem summable_norm_criticalPrimeTailComplexLaplaceAtom_iff (z : ℂ) :
    Summable (fun n : DeningerPrimePowerIndex =>
      ‖(criticalPrimeTailAtomWeight n : ℂ) *
        Complex.exp (-(z * (deningerPrimePowerTime n : ℂ)))‖) ↔
      1 / 2 < z.re := by
  have hpoint : (fun n : DeningerPrimePowerIndex =>
      ‖(criticalPrimeTailAtomWeight n : ℂ) *
        Complex.exp (-(z * (deningerPrimePowerTime n : ℂ)))‖) =
      criticalPrimeTailLaplaceMass z.re := by
    funext n
    rw [norm_mul, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_eq_abs,
      abs_of_nonneg (criticalPrimeTailAtomWeight_nonneg n), Complex.norm_exp]
    congr 2
    simp [Complex.mul_re]
  rw [hpoint, summable_criticalPrimeTailLaplaceMass_iff]

/-- At positive real Laplace rate, atomwise Green absolute Fubini is possible exactly to the right
of the same half-density wall. -/
theorem summable_integral_norm_exp_mul_zeroGreenAtom_iff
    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
    Summable (fun n : DeningerPrimePowerIndex =>
      ∫ L : ℝ, ‖Complex.exp (-((r : ℂ) * (L : ℂ))) *
        criticalPrimeTailZeroGreenAtom n L‖) ↔
      1 / 2 < r := by
